At such temperatures, the underside of the drop vaporizes at once, forming a thin cushion of steam.
The steam layer conducts heat poorly, so it slows the transfer of heat from the pan to the drop.
items.stem: The student wants to contrast the behavior of water drops on moderately hot and very hot pans and explain the difference. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A drop that boils away in seconds on a moderately hot pan can last a minute on a much hotter one, where a poorly conducting steam cushion forms beneath it.
choices.B: Whereas a water drop boils away within seconds on a pan just above water's boiling point, it can last a minute or more on a much hotter pan.
choices.C: Water drops that last longer on very hot pans are an example of the Leidenfrost effect, named for a German doctor who described it in 1756.
choices.D: A drop of water on a pan above roughly 200 °C rests on a thin cushion of steam, which conducts heat poorly and slows the flow of heat from the pan.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: contrast what happens on the two pans (seconds versus a minute or more) and explain why (a steam cushion that conducts heat poorly forms on the hotter pan). Only one choice includes the contrast and the explanation.
explanation.A: Correct. It contrasts the two pans and explains the difference with the poorly conducting steam cushion.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It states the contrast clearly but does not explain why it happens. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It names and dates the effect but neither describes the contrast in detail nor explains it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It explains what happens on the very hot pan but never contrasts it with a cooler pan.

items.subject: humanities
notes: In the mid-1880s, Japanese woodblock prints became widely available and popular in Paris.
Vincent van Gogh collected hundreds of these prints.
In 1887, he painted copies of two prints by Utagawa Hiroshige, one of which shows a plum tree in bloom.
In his copies, Van Gogh replaced Hiroshige's flat, even colors with thick, visible brushstrokes.
He also added borders filled with Japanese characters copied from other prints, apparently without knowing what they meant.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize that Van Gogh changed Hiroshige's prints when copying them, citing two different changes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In the mid-1880s, Japanese woodblock prints, including those of Hiroshige, became widely available and popular among collectors in Paris.
choices.B: In 1887, Van Gogh painted copies of two prints by Hiroshige in which he replaced the artist's flat, even colors with thick, visible brushstrokes.
choices.C: Copying Hiroshige in 1887, Van Gogh swapped flat colors for thick brushstrokes and added borders of Japanese characters he likely could not read.
choices.D: Van Gogh, who collected hundreds of Japanese woodblock prints, painted copies in 1887 of two prints by Hiroshige, including one of a plum tree in bloom.

explanation.why: The goal asks for two different changes Van Gogh made. The notes give two: he replaced flat colors with thick brushstrokes, and he added borders of copied Japanese characters. Only one choice cites both.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It describes the prints' popularity in Paris, not Van Gogh's copies.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It cites one change, the brushstrokes, but the goal asks for two. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Correct. It cites two changes: thick brushstrokes in place of flat color and added borders of Japanese characters.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It says Van Gogh copied the prints but does not mention any change he made.

items.subject: history_social
notes: Vijayanagara, in present-day Karnataka, India, was the capital of a powerful South Indian empire from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century.
Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveler, visited the city around 1520.
Paes wrote that the city was as large as Rome and described markets overflowing with rice, fruit, and precious stones.
Historians caution that travelers' accounts of distant cities can exaggerate.
Archaeological surveys at the site, now called Hampi, have mapped extensive remains of markets, temples, and water channels.
The city was largely abandoned after it was sacked in 1565.
items.stem: The student wants to present Paes's description of Vijayanagara and note a reason historians treat such descriptions with caution. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Archaeological surveys at Hampi, the site of Vijayanagara, have mapped extensive remains of the markets, temples, and water channels that Paes may have seen on his visit around 1520.
choices.B: Domingo Paes, who visited around 1520, likened Vijayanagara's size to Rome's, though historians warn that travelers' accounts of distant cities can exaggerate.
choices.C: Historians caution that travelers' accounts of distant cities, such as Vijayanagara, the capital of a South Indian empire, can be exaggerated.
choices.D: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveler, wrote that Vijayanagara was as large as Rome and that its markets overflowed with rice, fruit, and precious stones.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: present what Paes said about the city and give a reason for caution. The notes provide both: Paes compared the city's size to Rome's, and historians warn that travelers' accounts can exaggerate.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It describes archaeological evidence, which neither presents Paes's description nor gives a reason for caution.
explanation.B: Correct. It presents Paes's comparison to Rome and pairs it with the historians' warning about exaggeration.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It gives the reason for caution but never presents what Paes wrote.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It presents Paes's description fully but gives no reason for caution. This is the most attractive near miss.

items.subject: science
notes: The Venus flower basket is a deep-sea sponge whose skeleton is a lattice of fibers made of silica, the main ingredient of glass.
Fibers at the base of the sponge can be several centimeters long and about as thin as a human hair.
Researchers found that these fibers transmit light much as commercial optical fibers do.
Unlike commercial glass fibers, which snap easily when bent, the sponge's fibers can be bent sharply without breaking.
Their flexibility comes from layers of silica separated by thin layers of organic material.
Commercial optical fibers are made at very high temperatures, while the sponge forms its fibers in the cold water of the deep sea.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize two advantages that the sponge's fibers have over commercial optical fibers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Unlike commercial optical fibers, the sponge's fibers bend sharply without breaking, and they form in cold water rather than at high heat.
choices.B: Unlike commercial optical fibers, which snap easily when bent, the Venus flower basket's fibers can be bent sharply without breaking.
choices.C: The sponge's fibers bend sharply without breaking because their layers of silica are separated by thin layers of organic material.
choices.D: Like commercial optical fibers, the fibers at the base of the Venus flower basket, a deep-sea sponge, can transmit light along their length.

explanation.why: The goal asks for two advantages over commercial fibers. The notes give two: the sponge's fibers bend without breaking, and they form in cold water rather than requiring very high temperatures. Only one choice names both.
explanation.A: Correct. It names both advantages: the fibers bend without breaking, and they form without high heat.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It states one advantage clearly but omits the second. This is the most attractive near miss because it uses a direct comparison.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It explains the source of one advantage, flexibility, but names only that one and makes no comparison with commercial fibers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It describes a similarity between the fibers, not an advantage.

items.subject: humanities
notes: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are a group of more than 700 natural shelters in sandstone hills in central India.
Many of the shelters contain paintings, mostly in red and white, showing animals, hunting scenes, and dancing.
The oldest paintings are thought to be at least 10,000 years old, while others were made in much later periods.
Archaeologist V. S. Wakankar brought the shelters to scholars' attention in 1957.
In 2003, UNESCO named Bhimbetka a World Heritage Site.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce the Bhimbetka rock shelters to an unfamiliar audience and emphasize the long span of time over which their paintings were made. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The oldest of the paintings in the Bhimbetka rock shelters are thought to have been made at least 10,000 years ago.
choices.B: Bhimbetka, a group of more than 700 rock shelters in the sandstone hills of central India, holds paintings, mostly in red and white, of animals, hunting scenes, and dancing.
choices.C: Brought to scholars' attention by V. S. Wakankar in 1957, the Bhimbetka rock shelters of central India became a World Heritage Site in 2003.
choices.D: Bhimbetka, a group of rock shelters in central India, holds paintings made over a vast span of time, from at least 10,000 years ago to much later periods.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: introduce the site (what and where it is) and stress how long a period the paintings cover. The span runs from at least 10,000 years ago to much later periods. Only one choice introduces the site and presents that full span.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It gives the age of the oldest paintings, but an age is not a span, and it does not introduce the site to a reader who has never heard of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It introduces the site and describes the paintings but says nothing about when they were made. This is the most attractive near miss because it is the fullest introduction.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It gives the site's modern history, not the period over which the paintings were made.
explanation.D: Correct. It identifies the site and stresses the span of time from the oldest paintings to much later ones.

items.subject: history_social
notes: Tabulating the 1880 US census by hand took about eight years.
Officials feared that, with a rapidly growing population, the 1890 census would not be finished before the 1900 census began.
Engineer Herman Hollerith designed a machine that recorded census data as holes punched in cards and counted them electrically.
Using Hollerith's machines, the Census Office announced a total population count for 1890 within months.
Hollerith's company later became part of the firm that was renamed IBM in 1924.
items.stem: The student wants to explain the problem that Hollerith's machine addressed and how the machine addressed it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Officials feared that the 1890 census, like the 1880 one that took eight years to tabulate by hand, would not be finished before the next one began.
choices.B: Herman Hollerith, whose company later became part of the firm renamed IBM in 1924, designed a machine that recorded data as holes punched in cards.
choices.C: Using Hollerith's machines, which recorded data as holes punched in cards, the Census Office announced a population count for 1890 within months.
choices.D: Facing a census that might take a decade to tally by hand, officials turned to Hollerith's machine, which counted data punched into cards electrically.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: the problem (hand tabulation was so slow that the 1890 count might not finish before 1900) and the solution (a machine that counted data punched into cards electrically). Only one choice links the problem to the way the machine solved it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It describes the problem but not the machine that addressed it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It gives Hollerith's later business history and part of how the machine worked, but not the problem it addressed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It describes the machine and its result but never states the problem it was meant to solve. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.D: Correct. It states the problem (a census that might take a decade by hand) and how the machine addressed it (counting punched-card data electrically).

items.subject: science
items.passage: A vacuum flask keeps a drink hot for hours because of its double wall. Most of the air has been removed from the space between the inner and outer walls. Since heat travels through air by conduction and convection, this nearly empty space slows the escape of heat. Many flasks also have shiny inner surfaces, which reflect heat radiation back toward the drink.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the design of a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot
choices.B: To argue that vacuum flasks are better than all other containers
choices.C: To describe the shiny inner surfaces found in some flasks
choices.D: To compare conduction and convection as ways that heat travels

explanation.why: The first sentence states the idea ("A vacuum flask keeps a drink hot for hours because of its double wall"), and every later sentence explains a feature of the flask that slows heat loss. So the text's purpose is to explain how the flask's design works.
explanation.A: Correct. The whole text explains how the flask's features, the airless space and the shiny surfaces, keep heat in.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares flasks with other containers or argues that one is best.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The shiny surfaces are mentioned only in the last sentence; they are one detail, not the main purpose.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Conduction and convection are named only to explain why the empty space helps; the text does not compare them.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Every evening Amara's grandfather walked to the end of the pier with his fishing rod, though he rarely caught anything. One night Amara asked him why he kept going. He did not answer right away. Instead, he pointed at the orange sky sinking into the water and the gulls settling on the wooden posts. "The fish are only my excuse," he said, smiling. "This is what I come for."
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe how the grandfather taught Amara to fish
choices.B: To show that the grandfather is unhappy about catching so few fish
choices.C: To reveal the grandfather's real reason for his evening walks to the pier
choices.D: To explain why so few fish can be caught from the pier

explanation.why: The text sets up a puzzle (the grandfather goes every night "though he rarely caught anything") and then answers it: he points to the sunset and says, "The fish are only my excuse." The passage builds toward revealing why he really goes.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The grandfather never teaches Amara anything about fishing in the text.
explanation.B: Incorrect. He is "smiling" and says the fish are only an excuse, so he is not unhappy about catching few.
explanation.C: Correct. The story's point is his answer: he goes to the pier to enjoy the sunset and the gulls, not to catch fish.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says he rarely catches fish but never explains why the pier has few fish.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Anuradhapura, which served as a capital of Sri Lanka for more than a thousand years, is best known today for its enormous Buddhist stupas. Its reservoirs are equally revealing. <u>Some of these artificial lakes, called tanks, covered hundreds of hectares and were linked by canals that carried water many kilometers to fields on the dry plains.</u> Works on this scale suggest that the city's rulers could organize large numbers of laborers over many years, though exactly how that labor was recruited and directed is still debated.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It states the text's main conclusion about how Anuradhapura's rulers governed.
choices.B: It gives specific evidence for the inference drawn in the next sentence.
choices.C: It suggests that the reservoirs were less important than the city's stupas.
choices.D: It explains how the canals were built and who carried out the work.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence describes the size of the tanks and canals. The next sentence begins "Works on this scale suggest…" and draws a conclusion from that description. So the underlined sentence supplies the evidence and the following sentence states the inference.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The conclusion (that rulers could organize many laborers) comes in the following sentence; the underlined sentence is the evidence for it, not the conclusion itself.
explanation.B: Correct. The huge tanks and long canals are the evidence from which the next sentence infers that rulers "could organize large numbers of laborers."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text calls the reservoirs "equally revealing," so it does not rank them below the stupas.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence describes the size of the works, and the text says how the labor was organized "is still debated."

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The harpsichord, the leading keyboard instrument of the late 1600s, had a notable limitation: because its strings are plucked by a mechanism, a player cannot make a note louder or softer by pressing a key harder. Around 1700, the instrument maker Bartolomeo Cristofori in Florence solved this problem with a keyboard in which small hammers strike the strings, so the force of the player's touch controls the volume. His instrument's original name, gravicembalo col piano e forte, roughly "harpsichord with soft and loud," announced exactly this advantage, and its shortened form, "piano," survives today.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes an instrument and then explains why that instrument gradually fell out of use.
choices.B: It presents a claim about an inventor and then offers evidence that challenges it.
choices.C: It compares the sounds of two instruments and then argues that one is superior.
choices.D: It identifies a limitation of an instrument and then explains how an invention addressed it.

explanation.why: The first sentence names a problem with the harpsichord: a player "cannot make a note louder or softer." The second sentence says Cristofori "solved this problem" with hammers, and the third shows the new instrument's name advertised the solution. The text moves from a limitation to its solution.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never says the harpsichord fell out of use; it focuses on the problem the piano solved.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text challenges Cristofori's achievement; the name of his instrument supports it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text explains a mechanical difference in volume control; it does not compare the instruments' sounds or argue that one is better overall.
explanation.D: Correct. The text identifies the harpsichord's limitation and then explains how Cristofori's hammer mechanism overcame it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Sleep has usually been studied as a function of the brain, so a 2017 report that the upside-down jellyfish Cassiopea, which has no brain at all, enters a sleeplike state at night surprised many biologists. The jellyfish pulse less often at night and respond more slowly to stimuli, and when they are kept from resting, they are less active the following day, as if making up for lost rest. <u>Whether this state is sleep in the same sense that mammals sleep is harder to say, however, since the criteria the researchers applied were behavioral and reveal nothing about what happens inside the animal's simple nerve net.</u> Even so, the finding has led researchers to ask whether sleep arose far earlier in animal evolution than once assumed.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It qualifies the finding's significance by noting a limit of the evidence behind it.
choices.B: It rejects the claim that the jellyfish have a sleeplike state because of flawed observations.
choices.C: It explains how the researchers measured the jellyfish's responses to stimuli.
choices.D: It provides further evidence that the jellyfish's state resembles mammalian sleep.

explanation.why: Before the underlined sentence, the text reports behavioral evidence for a sleeplike state. The underlined sentence, signaled by "however," says the evidence cannot show whether this is sleep "in the same sense that mammals sleep" because it was only behavioral. It limits how far the finding can be taken without rejecting it, and the final sentence ("Even so") returns to the finding's importance.
explanation.A: Correct. The sentence accepts the behavioral evidence but points out what it cannot reveal, which narrows the finding's significance.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence does not reject the sleeplike state or criticize how the jellyfish were observed; it only says behavioral criteria cannot settle whether the state equals mammalian sleep. This goes further than the text.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sentence says the criteria were behavioral but does not explain how any responses were measured.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence raises doubt about the comparison with mammalian sleep; it does not add evidence for it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When the new conductor arrived, the orchestra's oldest violinist, Ilse Brandt, had already decided to dislike him. He was too young, she told the others, and he waved his arms as if he were directing traffic. At the first rehearsal she played precisely what was written and nothing more, watching him over the top of her music with an expression she had perfected over thirty years. But midway through the slow movement he stopped the orchestra, turned to her, and asked, quietly, as though it were a real question, how she would phrase the passage. Ilse found, to her irritation, that she had an answer, and that she wanted very much to give it.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show how the conductor's talent quickly wins over every member of the orchestra
choices.B: To depict a moment when a character's fixed hostility begins, against her will, to soften
choices.C: To explain why experienced musicians tend to distrust young conductors
choices.D: To describe the playing techniques Ilse has developed over her long career

explanation.why: Ilse begins having "already decided to dislike" the conductor. The turn comes with "But," when he sincerely asks her opinion, and she finds "to her irritation" that she "wanted very much" to answer. The passage captures her resistance starting to give way even though she does not want it to.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text shows only Ilse's reaction; it says nothing about the rest of the orchestra, and Ilse is not fully won over.
explanation.B: Correct. Ilse's settled dislike starts to weaken when the conductor asks for her view, and "to her irritation" shows this happens against her wishes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text is about one violinist and one conductor; it does not make a general claim about musicians.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Ilse's practiced expression and exact playing are details used to show her attitude, not the focus of the passage.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: It is sometimes said that Renaissance painters, by adopting linear perspective, at last learned to depict the world as the eye actually sees it. The claim has an obvious appeal: a painting constructed so that parallel lines converge on a single vanishing point can produce, for a viewer standing in the right place, a remarkably convincing illusion of depth. But the qualification in that sentence is doing considerable work. Linear perspective models what a single, motionless eye would register, whereas human beings look with two eyes that move constantly and a brain that assembles many glances into one impression. Perspective, on this view, is less a discovery of how vision works than an ingenious convention, one that succeeds because viewers have learned to accept its terms.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It introduces a claim, raises an objection to it, and then concedes that the objection fails for viewers in the correct position.
choices.B: It states a common view, dismisses it as baseless, and then offers a scientific account of two-eyed vision to replace it.
choices.C: It states a common view, grants the basis of its appeal, and then uses a condition within that basis to reinterpret the technique.
choices.D: It contrasts two Renaissance theories of vision and then explains why one of them came to dominate painting.

explanation.why: The text opens with a claim that perspective shows the world "as the eye actually sees it," then admits its appeal: perspective is convincing "for a viewer standing in the right place." The author then says "the qualification in that sentence is doing considerable work," turning that condition (one fixed viewpoint) into the reason to treat perspective as a "convention" rather than a discovery about vision.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the order of the argument. The appeal tied to the "right place" is granted first, and the objection that follows is not withdrawn; the text ends by reinterpreting perspective.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The author grants that the claim has "an obvious appeal" rather than calling it baseless, and the replacement offered is the idea of perspective as a convention, not a scientific account of vision.
explanation.C: Correct. The author grants why the view is appealing, then points to the condition built into that appeal (a single, still viewpoint) to recast perspective as a convention.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text discusses one technique and one popular claim about it, not two competing Renaissance theories.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Before the 1880s, most American towns kept their own local time, set by the position of the sun, so that clocks in neighboring cities might differ by several minutes. For railroads coordinating hundreds of trains, the result was a tangle of conflicting timetables. On November 18, 1883, the major railroads of the United States and Canada simply adopted a system of standard time zones on their own. <u>The federal government did not make those zones law until 1918, some thirty-five years later.</u> That sequence complicates a familiar assumption about how standards come about: here, a private arrangement devised to solve a practical problem established the national rule that public authority later merely confirmed.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It states the central argument that the final sentence then illustrates with an example.
choices.B: It suggests that the railroads' time zones were unpopular until the government required them.
choices.C: It qualifies the claim that the railroads acted on their own by noting that they needed legal approval.
choices.D: It supplies a detail about timing that the author uses to challenge a common view of how standards arise.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence gives a date: the zones became law only in 1918, long after the railroads adopted them in 1883. The final sentence begins "That sequence complicates a familiar assumption," so the author uses this timing to argue that a private arrangement, not government action, set the standard.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The underlined sentence is a factual detail; the argument appears in the final sentence, which draws on that detail rather than illustrating it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the time zones were unpopular. The author's point is that the railroads' system already worked as the national rule.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The railroads did not need approval; the law came thirty-five years later and "merely confirmed" what they had done. This choice reverses the sentence's point.
explanation.D: Correct. The thirty-five-year gap is the evidence the author uses to challenge the assumption that standards begin with public authority.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The platypus, an egg-laying mammal of eastern Australia, hunts along the bottoms of streams with its eyes, ears, and nostrils tightly closed. It finds food using its soft, rubbery bill, which is covered with tens of thousands of tiny sensors. Some of these sensors respond to touch, while others pick up the weak electric signals given off by the muscles of moving prey such as shrimp and insect larvae.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the platypus locates prey without using its eyes
choices.B: To describe the shrimp and insect larvae that live in Australian streams
choices.C: To compare the platypus with other mammals that lay eggs
choices.D: To argue that the platypus is the most skilled hunter in Australian streams

explanation.why: The first sentence sets up a puzzle: the platypus hunts "with its eyes, ears, and nostrils tightly closed." The rest of the text answers it by explaining that sensors on the bill detect touch and the "weak electric signals" of prey. So the text mainly explains how the platypus finds food without sight.
explanation.A: Correct. The text explains that the platypus closes its eyes underwater and relies on touch and electric sensors in its bill to find prey.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Shrimp and insect larvae are named only as examples of prey; the text does not describe them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text mentions that the platypus lays eggs but never compares it with any other egg-laying mammal.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text explains how the platypus hunts; it never ranks it against other hunters, so this claims far more than the text does.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: For a week, Mateo worked on his grandfather's old radio at the kitchen table. He replaced a cracked wire, cleaned the dusty dials, and tightened every loose screw. <u>Still, when he finally turned the knob, the radio gave only a faint hiss.</u> Mateo sighed and began to pack up his tools. Then his grandfather reached over, tapped the side of the case twice, and music suddenly filled the room.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes the first of several repairs that Mateo makes to the radio.
choices.B: It presents a letdown that comes just before the radio suddenly starts to play.
choices.C: It explains why Mateo's grandfather wanted the old radio repaired.
choices.D: It shows that Mateo does not have the skills he would need to repair the radio.

explanation.why: Before the underlined sentence, Mateo has worked for a week on the radio. The underlined sentence, beginning with "Still," tells us his efforts seem to have failed: the radio gives "only a faint hiss." Right after, the grandfather taps the case and "music suddenly filled the room," so the sentence sets up a letdown that the ending reverses.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The repairs are described in the sentence before; the underlined sentence tells what happened after they were finished.
explanation.B: Correct. The sentence describes the apparent failure of Mateo's work, which is then followed by the surprise of the radio playing.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never says why the grandfather wanted the radio fixed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The radio does work in the end, and nothing suggests Mateo's repairs were wrong, so this goes further than the text.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1974, farmers digging a well near the city of Xi'an, China, struck pieces of baked clay. The fragments turned out to belong to life-size statues of soldiers. Archaeologists have since uncovered thousands of these figures, which were buried more than 2,000 years ago near the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of a unified China. Each soldier's face is slightly different, and many once held real bronze weapons.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It presents a problem archaeologists faced and then the solution they found.
choices.B: It recounts an accidental discovery and then describes what it revealed.
choices.C: It argues that the clay statues are more important than the emperor's tomb.
choices.D: It describes an emperor's rise to power and then the building of his tomb.

explanation.why: The text begins with farmers who were digging a well and "struck pieces of baked clay" by chance. It then explains what the pieces turned out to be and describes the statues: thousands of soldiers, each with a different face and once holding real weapons. So the text moves from an accidental find to what the find showed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. No problem facing archaeologists is described; the text reports a discovery, not a solution.
explanation.B: Correct. The text tells how farmers found clay pieces by accident and then describes the army of statues they belonged to.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never compares the importance of the statues and the tomb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Qin Shi Huang is named, but the text never describes how he rose to power or how his tomb was built.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Katajjaq is a traditional vocal game of the Inuit of northern Canada. Two women stand face to face, often very close together, and take turns making quick, rhythmic sounds from the throat and chest. One singer sets a pattern, and the other answers with a different sound that fits around it. The game usually ends when one woman runs out of breath or starts to laugh, and the other is declared the winner.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show that katajjaq singers rarely enjoy taking part in the game
choices.B: To argue that katajjaq is more difficult than any other kind of singing
choices.C: To describe how a traditional Inuit vocal game is performed
choices.D: To explain how the Inuit first learned to make sounds from the throat

explanation.why: After naming katajjaq as "a traditional vocal game," every sentence explains a part of how it is played: how the two women stand, how they take turns, and how the game ends. So the main purpose is to describe how the game is performed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The game can end when a singer "starts to laugh," which suggests fun, not a lack of enjoyment.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares katajjaq with other kinds of singing.
explanation.C: Correct. The text explains who takes part, how they trade sounds, and how a winner is decided.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes the game as it is played; it says nothing about how throat sounds were first learned.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Mimosa pudica, a small plant native to Central and South America, is often called the sensitive plant. When an insect lands on it or a person brushes against it, its feathery leaves fold up within seconds. <u>The leaves move this way because water rapidly flows out of special cells at their bases, causing those cells to go limp.</u> After several minutes, the cells fill with water again and the leaves reopen.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes the insects that most often land on the plant.
choices.B: It explains why the leaves move as the previous sentence describes.
choices.C: It suggests that the leaves stay folded once they have closed.
choices.D: It introduces a second kind of plant whose leaves fold up in the same way.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one describes what happens: the leaves "fold up within seconds" when touched. The underlined sentence begins "The leaves move this way because," so it gives the reason for that movement: water leaving cells at the leaf bases.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Insects are mentioned only as one thing that can touch the plant; no insects are described.
explanation.B: Correct. The sentence explains why the leaves fold: water flows out of cells at their bases and the cells go limp.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence says the leaves "reopen" after several minutes, so they do not stay folded.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence is still about Mimosa pudica; no second plant is introduced.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The Inca Empire stretched along the steep slopes of the Andes Mountains in South America, where flat farmland was scarce. To grow enough food, Inca farmers built terraces: wide steps cut into the hillsides and held up by stone walls. The terraces created level fields, and their layers of gravel and soil let rainwater drain slowly instead of washing the hillside away.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It explains how rainwater damaged Inca fields and why the terraces failed.
choices.B: It argues that terraces were the greatest achievement of the Inca Empire.
choices.C: It describes the borders of the Inca Empire and then lists the crops it grew.
choices.D: It names a difficulty farmers faced and explains how they dealt with it.

explanation.why: The first sentence names a difficulty: in the steep Andes, "flat farmland was scarce." The next sentences explain the farmers' response, terraces that "created level fields" and kept rain from washing hillsides away. The text moves from a problem to its solution.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the terraces kept rainwater from washing the hillside away, so they succeeded rather than failed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text explains how terraces worked but never ranks them among the empire's achievements.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text names the Andes but never lists the empire's borders or its crops.
explanation.D: Correct. The text first describes the lack of flat land and then explains how terraces solved that problem.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Every Sunday morning, Dilini watched her grandmother press rice dough through a small metal mold, making thin strings that fell in neat circles onto a woven tray. Dilini's own attempts always came out lumpy and broken. This Sunday, her grandmother simply placed the mold in Dilini's hands and stepped back. Dilini pressed slowly and evenly, and a perfect circle of noodles formed. Her grandmother nodded once, smiling.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show that Dilini's grandmother is disappointed in her
choices.B: To list the ingredients needed to prepare a traditional dish
choices.C: To portray the moment Dilini succeeds at a task she found hard
choices.D: To explain why Dilini's grandmother prefers to cook by herself

explanation.why: The text first tells us that Dilini's attempts "always came out lumpy and broken." Then, on this Sunday, she makes "a perfect circle," and her grandmother nods with a smile. The passage builds toward that moment of success.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The grandmother nods "smiling," which shows approval, not disappointment.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Rice dough is mentioned, but the text does not list ingredients; it focuses on Dilini's experience.
explanation.C: Correct. The text contrasts Dilini's earlier failures with her success this Sunday, which her grandmother approves.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The grandmother hands Dilini the mold, so the text does not suggest she prefers to cook alone.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Many people believe that goldfish can remember things for only a few seconds. Experiments suggest otherwise. In several studies, goldfish were trained to swim to a certain spot whenever they heard a particular sound, which signaled feeding time. Weeks or even months later, many of the fish still responded to the sound, showing that they remembered what it meant.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It explains a scientific method and then lists several of its weaknesses.
choices.B: It reports experiments that confirmed what most people already believed.
choices.C: It describes how goldfish are fed and then explains why they need sound to find food.
choices.D: It presents a common belief and then gives evidence that the belief is mistaken.

explanation.why: The first sentence states what "many people believe": goldfish remember for only a few seconds. The second sentence, "Experiments suggest otherwise," signals a challenge, and the rest describes fish that remembered a sound for "weeks or even months." The text sets up a belief and then disproves it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text describes experiments but never discusses any weaknesses in them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The experiments go against the popular belief; they do not confirm it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sound is part of an experiment on memory; the text never says goldfish need sound to find food.
explanation.D: Correct. The text states the popular belief about goldfish memory and then describes experiments showing it is wrong.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Papel picado, which means "perforated paper" in Spanish, is a Mexican folk art in which designs are cut into thin tissue paper. Artisans stack dozens of sheets and cut through them all at once with small chisels. <u>The finished sheets are strung together into colorful banners that are hung over streets and doorways during celebrations such as the Day of the Dead.</u> Because the paper is so delicate, the banners usually last only a short time.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains how artisans cut designs into stacks of paper.
choices.B: It suggests that the banners are made to be kept for many years.
choices.C: It describes how the finished cut paper is displayed and used.
choices.D: It argues that papel picado is the most popular art form in Mexico.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one explains how the designs are cut. The underlined sentence moves to what happens next: the sheets become banners "hung over streets and doorways during celebrations." Its role is to show how the finished paper is used.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The cutting is described in the sentence before; the underlined sentence is about the finished sheets.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The last sentence says the banners "usually last only a short time," the opposite of this choice.
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence tells how the sheets are strung into banners and hung during celebrations.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never compares papel picado with other Mexican art forms.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The banyan, the national tree of India, grows in an unusual way. As its branches spread outward, they send down thin roots that hang in the air. When these roots reach the ground, they take hold in the soil and slowly thicken into woody pillars that look like extra trunks. Held up by these pillars, a single banyan can stretch its branches over a huge area.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the many ways people have used banyan roots
choices.B: To explain how the banyan tree is able to spread so widely
choices.C: To argue that the banyan is the most important tree in India
choices.D: To describe how the banyan's roots look before they touch the soil

explanation.why: The text says the banyan "grows in an unusual way" and then traces the process: hanging roots reach the soil, become pillars, and hold up branches over "a huge area." The whole text explains how the tree manages to spread so far.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text describes how the roots help the tree grow; it never mentions people using them.
explanation.B: Correct. The text explains how hanging roots turn into supporting pillars that let the branches spread over a wide area.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text calls the banyan India's national tree but never argues that it is the most important tree.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The hanging roots are only one stage in the process the text explains, not its main focus.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When the family next door got a puppy, Mr. Okonjo was annoyed. The puppy barked at the mail carrier, dug under the fence, and once ran off with one of his garden gloves. Then, one rainy afternoon, he found it shivering on his doorstep, lost and soaked. He dried it with a towel, gave it some water, and was surprised to feel sorry when its owners came to take it home.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes a character's daily routine and then explains why he decided to move to a new home.
choices.B: It compares the habits of two dogs that live in the same neighborhood.
choices.C: It presents a character's irritation with a pet and then an event that changes his feelings.
choices.D: It shows a character's anger growing until he complains to his neighbors about a pet.

explanation.why: The text opens with Mr. Okonjo "annoyed" and lists the puppy's misdeeds. The word "Then" introduces a turning point: he cares for the lost, soaked puppy and is "surprised to feel sorry" when it leaves. The structure moves from irritation to warmer feelings.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never describes Mr. Okonjo's routine or says that he moved.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Only one puppy appears in the text.
explanation.C: Correct. Mr. Okonjo starts out annoyed by the puppy, but caring for it on a rainy day changes how he feels.
explanation.D: Incorrect. His feelings grow warmer, not angrier, and he never complains to the neighbors.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1783, the French brothers Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Étienne Montgolfier built a large cloth-and-paper balloon that rose when filled with hot air. That September, they sent up a sheep, a duck, and a rooster in a basket beneath it. <u>All three animals survived the flight, which lasted about eight minutes.</u> Encouraged, the brothers prepared a balloon for passengers, and in November two men made the first free flight by humans.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It suggests that the first flight with animals ended in failure.
choices.B: It reports the outcome of a test that led the brothers to their next step.
choices.C: It describes the materials the brothers used to build their balloon.
choices.D: It explains why the brothers decided to test the balloon with animals first.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one describes a test flight with animals, and the underlined sentence tells how it turned out: the animals "survived." The next sentence begins "Encouraged," showing that this result led the brothers to build a balloon for people.
explanation.A: Incorrect. All three animals survived, so the flight succeeded.
explanation.B: Correct. The animals' safe flight is the result that encouraged the brothers to try a flight with people.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The materials are named in the first sentence; the underlined sentence is about the outcome of the animal flight.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says why animals were sent up first.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Humans see color with three types of light-detecting cells, but mantis shrimp have twelve. For years, many biologists assumed that the shrimp must therefore be able to tell apart far more shades than people can. A 2014 study tested that assumption by training mantis shrimp to choose one color over another for a food reward. <u>The shrimp did poorly once the two colors were close in wavelength, failing at differences that humans notice easily.</u> The researchers concluded that the shrimp probably use their many cell types to recognize colors quickly rather than to compare them finely.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It offers evidence that mantis shrimp distinguish more shades than humans do.
choices.B: It presents the assumption that the study was designed to test.
choices.C: It describes how the shrimp were trained to choose between colors.
choices.D: It reports a result that runs counter to a widely held assumption.

explanation.why: The text first states an assumption: with twelve cell types, the shrimp "must therefore be able to tell apart far more shades than people can." The underlined sentence reports what the study found: the shrimp failed at color differences "that humans notice easily." That result contradicts the assumption and leads to the researchers' different conclusion in the last sentence.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The shrimp did worse than humans at telling similar colors apart, so the sentence weakens this idea rather than supporting it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The assumption appears in the second sentence; the underlined sentence gives the study's result.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The training method is described in the sentence before; the underlined sentence tells how the shrimp performed.
explanation.D: Correct. The shrimp's poor performance with similar colors challenges the belief that more cell types meant finer color discrimination.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The Ajanta Caves, cut into a horseshoe-shaped cliff in western India, were carved and painted by Buddhist monks and artists between about the second century BCE and the fifth century CE. Their wall paintings show scenes from the lives of the Buddha alongside crowded palaces, markets, and forests. After the site was abandoned, it lay hidden by forest for centuries, until a British officer on a hunting trip came upon one of the caves in 1819. Today the paintings are valued not only as religious art but also as a rare record of everyday life, dress, and architecture in ancient India.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To introduce the Ajanta Caves and explain why their paintings are valued today
choices.B: To explain why Buddhist monks abandoned the Ajanta Caves after the fifth century
choices.C: To describe how a British officer came upon the caves while hunting in 1819
choices.D: To argue that the Ajanta paintings are the finest religious art ever produced in India

explanation.why: The text tells when and by whom the caves were made, what the paintings show, how the site was rediscovered, and finally why the paintings matter: they are valued as religious art and as "a rare record of everyday life." A choice must cover this overview and its point about the paintings' value.
explanation.A: Correct. The text presents the caves' history and contents and ends by explaining the two reasons the paintings are prized.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the site was abandoned but never gives a reason.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The officer's discovery is one detail in the history of the site, not the purpose of the whole text.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the paintings are valued, but it never ranks them against all other religious art in India.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: At the thirty-ninth kilometer, Ingrid's legs felt as though they had been filled with wet sand. Runners she had passed an hour earlier drifted by one after another, and she began working out how slowly she could walk and still finish before the course closed. Then, around a bend, she saw her younger brother standing on an overturned crate, waving a cardboard sign with her name painted on it in enormous, crooked letters. Ingrid laughed out loud, and without quite deciding to, she began to run again.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It presents a character's careful strategy for a race and then shows that strategy succeeding.
choices.B: It describes a character's growing discouragement and then an encounter that revives her.
choices.C: It shows a character's confidence early in a race and then its steady decline.
choices.D: It focuses on a sign that a character's brother made and how he made it.

explanation.why: The first two sentences show Ingrid exhausted and losing hope: other runners pass her and she plans to walk. "Then" marks a turn: seeing her brother's sign makes her laugh, and she starts running again. The text moves from discouragement to renewed effort.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Her only plan is to walk to the finish, and she abandons it when she starts running again, so no strategy succeeds.
explanation.B: Correct. Ingrid's fatigue and plan to walk give way, after she sees her brother's sign, to running again.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text begins with Ingrid already struggling and ends with her spirits lifting, the reverse of this pattern.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sign matters only for its effect on Ingrid; the text does not explain how it was made.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In 1919, the architect Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus, a school of art and design in Weimar, Germany. At the time, fine art and practical craft were usually taught separately: painters trained at academies, while furniture makers and weavers learned in workshops. Gropius wanted to end that division. Bauhaus students studied color and form with painters but also worked in metal, wood, and textile workshops, designing chairs, lamps, and teapots meant to be both beautiful and practical to manufacture. Although the school closed in 1933, its approach shaped design teaching around the world.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the Bauhaus departed from the usual training of artists
choices.B: To describe the events that forced the Bauhaus to close in 1933
choices.C: To compare how painters and furniture makers were each trained before 1919
choices.D: To argue that the Bauhaus produced better furniture than any earlier school

explanation.why: The text describes the usual practice of teaching art and craft "separately," says Gropius "wanted to end that division," and explains how Bauhaus students combined both. It closes by noting the approach's wide influence. The main purpose is to show how the school's training differed from the norm.
explanation.A: Correct. The text contrasts the old separation of art and craft with the Bauhaus's combined training.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text gives the year the school closed but not the events behind it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The separate training of painters and furniture makers is background for the Bauhaus's new approach, not the text's main focus.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says Bauhaus designs were meant to be beautiful and practical but never claims they were better than any earlier school's.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Play is usually studied in mammals and birds, but a team of zoologists wondered whether insects might play too. They built an arena in which bumblebees could walk straight to a feeding station or detour into an area scattered with small wooden balls. Many bees went out of their way to roll the balls, even though doing so earned them no food. <u>Younger bees rolled the balls more often than older ones, a pattern also seen in mammals, whose young tend to play more than adults.</u> The researchers argue that such results make it harder to treat play as limited to animals with large brains.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains why the bees received no food for rolling the balls.
choices.B: It suggests that older bees are better at finding food than younger bees.
choices.C: It raises a difficulty that weakens the researchers' conclusion about insect play.
choices.D: It notes a parallel that supports the view that the bees' behavior is play.

explanation.why: the researchers is testing whether insects "might play too." The underlined sentence notes that, as in mammals, young bees roll balls more than older ones. That similarity to a known pattern of play in mammals adds support to the idea that the ball rolling is play, which leads to her conclusion in the last sentence.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence compares younger and older bees; it says nothing about why rolling earned no food.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence is about how often bees rolled balls, not how well they found food, so this goes beyond the text.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sentence supports the researchers' conclusion rather than raising a problem for it.
explanation.D: Correct. The age pattern matches play in mammals, so it supports reading the bees' ball rolling as play.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the 1850s, most of London's sewage still flowed straight into the River Thames. Many doctors believed that diseases such as cholera spread through foul-smelling air, so the river's stench was a constant worry. In the unusually hot summer of 1858, the smell became so overpowering that members of Parliament, whose building stands on the riverbank, could barely work. Within weeks, they approved funding for engineer Joseph Bazalgette's plan for a vast network of sewers to carry waste away from the city center.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes an engineer's early career and then the project that made him famous.
choices.B: It focuses on the weather in 1858 and its effects on the River Thames.
choices.C: It traces how a long-standing problem finally pushed officials to approve a solution.
choices.D: It explains a theory about how disease spreads and then shows how it was proved correct.

explanation.why: The text begins with an ongoing problem: sewage in the Thames and fear of its smell. The hot summer of 1858 made the smell unbearable even for Parliament, and "within weeks" members approved a sewer plan. The text moves from a problem, to the event that brought it to a head, to the decision to fix it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Bazalgette appears only as the planner of the sewers; the text says nothing about his career.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The hot summer is one stage in the text; the text is about the sewage problem and Parliament's response.
explanation.C: Correct. The text shows how the long-standing sewage problem, made worse by the hot summer, led Parliament to fund the sewers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text reports that doctors believed bad air spread cholera but never says the belief was proved correct.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Bilal had spent three months at his uncle's workshop in Multan, and still he had not been allowed to paint a single tile. He mixed glazes, swept up clay dust, and watched his uncle's brush trace blue vines and flowers across white surfaces. One evening, Bilal complained that he was learning nothing. His uncle said nothing; he simply handed Bilal a brush and a blank tile. Bilal began, then stopped. Without thinking, he found himself pausing at each curve the way his uncle did, already knowing where the next leaf should go.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To reveal that Bilal has learned more by watching than he knew
choices.B: To show that Bilal's uncle is unwilling to teach him the craft
choices.C: To explain why Bilal decides to leave his uncle's workshop
choices.D: To describe the steps involved in making glazed tiles in Multan

explanation.why: Bilal complains that he is "learning nothing" because he has only mixed, swept, and watched. When his uncle hands him a brush, Bilal finds himself painting the way his uncle does, "already knowing where the next leaf should go." The passage shows that his months of watching taught him more than he realized.
explanation.A: Correct. When Bilal finally paints, he moves the way his uncle does, showing that watching taught him more than he believed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The uncle hands Bilal a brush and a tile, and Bilal's watching has already taught him, so the uncle is not refusing to teach.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Bilal complains, but the text never suggests that he decides to leave.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Mixing glazes and painting are mentioned, but the text does not explain how tiles are made; it focuses on Bilal's discovery.

items.subject: science
items.passage: On June 30, 1908, a huge explosion flattened about 80 million trees across more than 2,000 square kilometers of forest near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia. When scientists finally reached the remote site in 1927, they expected to find a large crater and pieces of a meteorite. They found neither. The trees near the center were still standing but stripped of branches, while those farther out lay pointing away from it. Most researchers now conclude that a space rock exploded several kilometers above the ground, so that the blast, rather than an impact, did the damage.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes an event's effects on nearby villages and then describes the forest's slow recovery.
choices.B: It describes a search for meteorite fragments and argues that the search should continue.
choices.C: It describes an event, notes evidence that defied expectations, and gives a current explanation.
choices.D: It explains how scientists predicted an explosion and then how its damage was limited.

explanation.why: The text first describes the 1908 explosion. Scientists who reached the site "expected to find a large crater" and meteorite pieces but "found neither," and the pattern of trees was puzzling. The last sentence gives the conclusion most researchers now accept: a space rock exploded in the air.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text describes fallen trees, not effects on villages, and says nothing about the forest's recovery.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says no meteorite pieces were found and offers an explanation for their absence; it does not call for more searching.
explanation.C: Correct. The text moves from the explosion, to the unexpected lack of a crater, to the airburst explanation researchers now favor.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says anyone predicted the explosion or limited its damage.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In 1901, divers exploring an ancient shipwreck near the Greek island of Antikythera recovered a lump of corroded bronze. At first, it attracted little attention. <u>Decades later, X-ray images revealed that the lump contained dozens of interlocking bronze gears, cut with a precision unknown in any other surviving object from the ancient world.</u> Researchers now believe the device, built more than 2,000 years ago, was turned by hand to show the positions of the Sun and Moon and to predict eclipses. Its complexity has forced historians to reconsider what ancient Greek engineers could achieve.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It reports the finding that transformed how the object was understood.
choices.B: It describes the methods the divers used to bring objects up from the wreck.
choices.C: It states the main conclusion that historians have drawn about Greek engineering.
choices.D: It shows that the object's importance was recognized as soon as it was found.

explanation.why: Before the underlined sentence, the bronze lump "attracted little attention." The underlined sentence reveals what X-rays showed inside it, precise gears unlike anything else from the ancient world. That discovery leads to the later sentences about what the device did and how it changed historians' views.
explanation.A: Correct. The X-rays turned an overlooked lump into evidence of a precise geared device, changing how the object was seen.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence is about X-ray images taken decades later, not about how the divers worked.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The conclusion about Greek engineers comes in the last sentence; the underlined sentence gives the discovery that led to it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the object "attracted little attention" at first; its importance was recognized only decades later.

items.subject: science
items.passage: On a few beaches along the coast of Odisha, in eastern India, olive ridley sea turtles nest in a remarkable way. Instead of arriving one by one, tens of thousands of females may come ashore over just a few nights to dig nests and lay eggs, an event known by the Spanish word arribada, or "arrival." <u>Biologists think this crowding may help the eggs survive, since predators such as jackals and crows can eat only a small share of so many eggs at once.</u> Exactly what signals the turtles to gather at the same time, however, is still not understood.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes how quickly the turtles arrive on the beaches.
choices.B: It suggests a possible reason for the behavior described just before it.
choices.C: It identifies the signal that causes the turtles to arrive together.
choices.D: It argues that predators are the greatest threat to the turtles' survival.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one describes the behavior: thousands of turtles nesting "over just a few nights." The underlined sentence gives a possible benefit of that crowding, hedged with "think" and "may": predators can eat only a small share of the eggs. The last sentence then notes what is still unknown.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The speed of the arrival is described in the previous sentence; the underlined sentence suggests why the crowding helps.
explanation.B: Correct. It offers a likely reason for mass nesting: so many eggs at once means predators can eat only a small share.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence says the signal "is still not understood," so the underlined sentence cannot identify it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence names predators but does not compare them with other threats, so this claims more than the text.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1325, Ibn Battuta, a young scholar from Tangier in Morocco, set out on a pilgrimage to Mecca. He did not return home for nearly twenty-five years, traveling through North and East Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, and possibly China. Back in Morocco, he dictated his memories to a writer, producing the book known as the Rihla. Historians value its vivid accounts of courts, cities, and customs, but they read it with care: some passages appear to borrow from earlier writers, and his account of China is especially uncertain.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To present a historical source and weigh its value and limits
choices.B: To argue that Ibn Battuta invented most of the journeys in the Rihla
choices.C: To describe the route Ibn Battuta followed on his way to Mecca
choices.D: To explain why Ibn Battuta waited so long before returning home

explanation.why: The text explains how the Rihla came to exist and then gives historians' view of it: they "value its vivid accounts" "but they read it with care" because of borrowed passages and doubts about China. The purpose is to introduce the source and weigh its strengths and weaknesses.
explanation.A: Correct. The text introduces the Rihla, praises its vivid detail, and notes reasons historians treat it cautiously.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says only that some passages seem borrowed and the China section is uncertain, not that most journeys were invented.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The pilgrimage to Mecca is only the starting point; the text never traces that route.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says how long he was away but never explains why.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: All evening the wind had been rising, and by midnight the waves were throwing spray against the windows of the lighthouse. Kirsten's father had gone down to the village for medicine and had not come back. Twice she climbed the iron stairs to trim the lamp's wick, just as she had watched him do a hundred times. <u>Each time, her hands shook so badly that she nearly dropped the scissors.</u> But each time the flame steadied and burned brighter, sending its beam out across the black water toward any ship that might be out there.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It shows that Kirsten cannot keep the lamp burning without her father.
choices.B: It reveals that the storm has damaged the lamp and its equipment.
choices.C: It conveys Kirsten's fear even as she succeeds at her task.
choices.D: It explains how Kirsten learned to trim the lamp's wick.

explanation.why: Kirsten is alone in a storm, tending the lamp as her father usually does. The underlined sentence shows her hands shaking with nerves, and the next sentence, starting with "But," shows that the flame still "steadied and burned brighter." The sentence highlights her fear, which the next sentence sets against her success.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The next sentence says the flame "steadied and burned brighter," so she does keep the lamp burning.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the storm damaged the lamp; the shaking comes from Kirsten's hands.
explanation.C: Correct. Her shaking hands show her fear, and the following sentence shows that she succeeds anyway.
explanation.D: Incorrect. How she learned (by watching her father) is told in the previous sentence; the underlined sentence describes her shaking hands.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Desert ants of the genus Cataglyphis forage across the flat, featureless sand of the Sahara, often wandering far from their nest before heading straight back to it. Researchers long suspected that the ants judge distance by counting their steps. To test this idea, one team trained ants to walk to a feeder and then altered their legs: some received tiny stilts made of pig bristles, while others had their legs shortened. On the way home, the ants on stilts overshot the nest and those with shortened legs stopped short of it, as expected if the ants measure distance by counting steps.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how desert ants locate sources of food far from the nest
choices.B: To argue that desert ants have a better sense of direction than any other insect
choices.C: To describe how the flat sand of the Sahara makes landmarks hard to find
choices.D: To describe an experiment that tested how desert ants judge distance

explanation.why: The text states a suspicion (the ants "judge distance by counting their steps"), describes how one team tested it with stilts and shortened legs, and reports results "as expected" if the idea is right. Its main purpose is to present that test of how the ants measure distance.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The experiment is about how the ants find their way home, not how they find food.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares desert ants with other insects.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The featureless sand is background that explains why the ants' navigation is interesting; it is not the focus.
explanation.D: Correct. Most of the text describes how researchers altered the ants' legs to test the step-counting idea and what happened.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In 1901, the poet Rabindranath Tagore opened a small school at Santiniketan, in rural Bengal. Tagore had disliked his own schooling in Calcutta, where he felt shut up in stuffy classrooms and drilled in memorization. At Santiniketan, by contrast, students often held lessons outdoors beneath the trees, and music, painting, and drama were treated as seriously as mathematics. The school later grew into Visva-Bharati, a university that drew students and teachers from many countries.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It focuses on how a university attracted students from many countries.
choices.B: It describes a poet's best-known works and the places that inspired them.
choices.C: It argues that outdoor lessons teach students more effectively than classroom lessons do.
choices.D: It contrasts a founder's own schooling with the kind of school he went on to create.

explanation.why: After naming the school, the text describes Tagore's unhappy schooling in "stuffy classrooms." The phrase "by contrast" introduces Santiniketan's outdoor lessons and focus on the arts. The text is built on a contrast between the education Tagore received and the one he created, ending with how the school grew.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Visva-Bharati's international reach appears only in the final sentence; it is not the text's organizing idea.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Tagore is called a poet, but the text never mentions any of his works.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text describes Santiniketan's outdoor lessons but never claims they are more effective in general.
explanation.D: Correct. The text sets Tagore's confined, memorization-based schooling against Santiniketan's outdoor, arts-rich lessons.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1085, nearly twenty years after conquering England, William the Conqueror ordered a survey of his kingdom. Royal officials traveled through almost every county, recording who held each piece of land, how many people worked it, and how many plows, mills, and animals it had. The results were compiled in the Domesday Book. The survey's main purpose was practical: it showed the king what each landholder owned and could be taxed. <u>For modern historians, however, its value lies elsewhere, since it offers an unusually detailed picture of ordinary life in eleventh-century England.</u>
items.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It restates the practical reason the king ordered the survey.
choices.B: It argues that many of the survey's tax records were inaccurate.
choices.C: It contrasts the survey's original purpose with the reason it is valued today.
choices.D: It describes the methods officials used to collect information for the survey.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one gives the survey's "main purpose": helping the king tax landholders. The underlined sentence, signaled by "however" and "its value lies elsewhere," shifts to why historians value it now: it shows "ordinary life in eleventh-century England." Its role is to set the modern value against the original aim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The underlined sentence moves away from the tax purpose ("its value lies elsewhere") rather than repeating it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never questions the accuracy of the survey's records.
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence sets the historians' reason for valuing the survey against the king's practical reason for ordering it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The officials' methods are described in the second sentence, not the underlined one.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In 1912, the German scientist Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined and had slowly drifted apart. He pointed to the way the coasts of South America and Africa seem to fit together and to matching fossils found on both sides of the Atlantic. Most geologists rejected the idea, largely because Wegener could not explain what force could move entire continents. Only in the 1960s, after studies of the ocean floor showed that new crust forms along mid-ocean ridges and spreads outward, did his central idea win wide acceptance.
items.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It explains how studies of the ocean floor led geologists to reject a theory.
choices.B: It compares the fossils of South America with those of Africa in detail.
choices.C: It describes a scientific debate and explains why that debate has never been fully settled.
choices.D: It presents an idea, explains its early rejection, and describes its later acceptance.

explanation.why: The text introduces Wegener's proposal and his evidence, then says most geologists "rejected the idea" because he had no mechanism. The last sentence explains that ocean-floor studies in the 1960s led the idea to "win wide acceptance." The text moves from proposal, to rejection, to acceptance.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The ocean-floor studies supported Wegener's idea; they did not lead geologists to reject it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The matching fossils are mentioned briefly as Wegener's evidence; they are not compared in detail.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence says Wegener's idea won wide acceptance, so the debate was largely settled.
explanation.D: Correct. The text presents continental drift, gives the reason it was first rejected, and explains how later evidence led to its acceptance.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Ravi had coached Lucía since she was eight, and for five years he had won every practice game they played. This afternoon, she moved her knight, looked up, and waited. Ravi studied the board, searching for an escape, and found none. He felt a brief sting of wounded pride, and then, to his own surprise, something much larger and warmer. He looked up at his student and, slowly, began to grin.
items.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how Lucía learned to play chess so skillfully
choices.B: To describe the chess move that allowed Lucía to win the game
choices.C: To show that Ravi is angry and embarrassed about losing to a student
choices.D: To portray Ravi's pride in his student outweighing his hurt

explanation.why: Ravi, who has always beaten Lucía, finds no escape from her move. He feels "a brief sting of wounded pride" but then "something much larger and warmer," and he grins. The passage centers on his reaction: a moment of hurt that gives way to pleasure in her success.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says Ravi has coached her for five years but never explains how she developed her skill.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The winning move is mentioned only briefly ("she moved her knight"); the text focuses on Ravi's feelings.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Ravi's wounded pride is "brief," and it is replaced by a warmer feeling and a grin, so anger is not the point.
explanation.D: Correct. The brief sting of losing gives way to a "larger and warmer" feeling, shown by Ravi's grin at his student.

items.subject: humanities
