His design succeeded where more than two hundred competition entries had failed largely because of a quality that had little to do with beauty: nearly every part of the building, from its cast-iron columns to its panes of glass, was made to a few standard sizes and could be produced in quantity at factories and bolted together on site. ______ the building was conceived less as a monument than as a kit, assembled from interchangeable pieces.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains in detail that the building's parts came in standard sizes, were made in factories, and were bolted together on site. The last sentence sums up that same idea in a single image: the building was a kit. A restatement transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The idea of a kit is not one example of standardized parts; it describes the whole building's design.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates the point about standardized, factory-made parts as the idea of a kit.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but calling the building a kit agrees with the description of standard, bolted parts. It is tempting because the kit image seems to downplay the building's grandeur.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a narrower, more detailed point, but the last sentence is a broader summary of the detail that came before. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The notebooks that Srinivasa Ramanujan kept before he left India for Cambridge in 1914 contain more than three thousand mathematical results, most stated without proof, a habit that troubled the professional mathematicians who later studied them. Some of the claims proved to be mistaken, and many rested on reasoning that Ramanujan never wrote down, leaving later scholars to reconstruct it step by step. ______ when mathematicians spent decades working systematically through the notebooks, they found that the great majority of the results were correct, and a number of them anticipated work that would not appear elsewhere for many years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe problems with the notebooks: results without proof, some mistakes, and missing reasoning. The last sentence reports that most of the results turned out to be correct. The transition must signal that this was true in spite of the problems just listed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that the results proved largely correct in spite of the missing proofs and occasional errors.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the problems, but the last sentence reaches the opposite verdict.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" would mean the correctness of the results resembles the problems just described, but it goes against them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Consequently" would mean the missing proofs and errors caused the results to be correct, which reverses the logic.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Few residents of the town could remember a time when the Misses Harrow had not quarreled, and fewer still could recall what the original quarrel had concerned. The two sisters, who had shared the narrow house on Crane Street for upward of forty years, communicated chiefly through the housemaid, and each took her meals at a different hour so as never to be found at the same table as the other. ______ so complete was their estrangement that when the elder fell ill one winter, the younger learned of it only from the doctor, whom she happened to meet upon the stairs.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Indeed,

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe how deeply the sisters were estranged. The last sentence pushes that description further with the most striking evidence of all: one did not know the other was ill. A transition that reinforces and intensifies the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but the illness episode confirms the estrangement rather than going against it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but the last sentence continues the same picture of the sisters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Consequently" would make the illness episode a result of the separate mealtimes and the messages through the housemaid, but all of these are signs of the same estrangement, and the last sentence presents the most extreme of them.
explanation.D: Correct. "Indeed" introduces an even stronger illustration of how complete the sisters' estrangement was.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Amir Khusrau, the poet and musician who served at the court of the Delhi Sultanate in the late thirteenth and early fourteenth centuries, is popularly credited with inventing the sitar, and the story is repeated in many concert programs and textbooks. Historians of music regard the claim as doubtful on two counts. First, no instrument called a sitar, or clearly resembling the modern one, is described in any surviving source until several centuries after Khusrau's death in 1325. ______ Khusrau's own extensive writings, which discuss the music and musicians of his time at considerable length, never mention such an instrument.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The second sentence says historians doubt the claim "on two counts," and the third sentence gives the first count. The last sentence gives the second, separate reason for doubt: Khusrau himself never mentions a sitar. A transition that adds another point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The silence of Khusrau's writings is not caused by the absence of the sitar from later sources; both are independent reasons for doubt.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds the silence of Khusrau's own writings as the second reason to doubt the claim.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the second reason replaces the first, but the historians hold both.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the first count, but the last sentence offers a separate piece of evidence, as "two counts" and "First" signal. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: science
items.passage: On Earth, the volcanoes of the Hawaiian Islands formed as the Pacific Plate moved slowly over a stationary plume of hot material rising from deep within the mantle; because the plate kept shifting, each volcano was eventually carried away from the plume and went extinct while a new one began to grow in its place. Mars, by contrast, shows no evidence of plate tectonics, and its crust appears to have remained fixed above its mantle plumes for very long periods. ______ lava erupting at a single site on Mars could keep piling up for hundreds of millions of years, building Olympus Mons, a volcano roughly two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The text explains that on Earth moving plates carry volcanoes away from their source, but that Mars's crust stayed fixed above its plumes. The last sentence gives the effect of that fixed crust: lava kept piling up in one place, creating an enormous volcano. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Consequently" shows that Olympus Mons grew so tall because Mars's crust stayed fixed above its plumes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In contrast" is tempting because the previous sentence uses "by contrast," but the Earth-Mars contrast is already made; the last sentence follows from Mars's fixed crust rather than contrasting with it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" means "in spite of that," but the huge volcano is what a fixed crust would lead us to expect.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" would mean Olympus Mons formed the way the Hawaiian volcanoes did, but the text stresses that the two processes differ.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: For centuries, the Icelandic sagas' accounts of Norse voyages to a land they called Vinland were treated by many historians as little more than legend. That view changed in the 1960s, when excavations at L'Anse aux Meadows, on the northern tip of Newfoundland, uncovered the remains of Norse-style buildings dated to around 1000 CE. ______ the settlement was small and seems to have been occupied for only a few years, so it cannot by itself show that the Norse established a lasting presence in North America; but it leaves no doubt that they arrived there roughly five centuries before Columbus.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Granted,
choices.B: Indeed,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The author's main point is that L'Anse aux Meadows proves the Norse reached North America. The blank sentence first admits a limitation (the site was small and short-lived) and then, with "but," returns to what the site does prove. A concession transition is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Granted" concedes the settlement's limits before the author insists, with "but," on what it proves.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Indeed" would strengthen the previous sentence, but the site's small size and short use limit what it shows. It is tempting because the sentence ends by supporting the main point.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The settlement's limits are not an example of the change in historians' views; they qualify that change.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The settlement's small size is not a result of its discovery in the 1960s.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The letter that arrived in March was addressed in a hand Oksana had not seen in nearly twenty years, and she left it unopened on the hall table for most of a week, walking past it each morning as though it were an ordinary bill. When at last she read it, she learned that her old piano teacher, now in her nineties, had heard Oksana's recording on the radio and wished to tell her how proud she was. ______ Oksana had believed that the teacher, who had dismissed her from lessons with the remark that she lacked discipline, had long since forgotten her, or remembered her only as a failure.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Afterward,
choices.D: Until then,

explanation.why: The last sentence uses "had believed," which describes what Oksana thought before she read the letter. The transition must mark that earlier time and show that the letter ended her old belief.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Oksana held her belief in spite of the letter, but the past perfect "had believed" refers to the time before the letter. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Her belief that the teacher had forgotten her is not a restatement of the letter's message; it is the opposite.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Afterward" would place her belief after reading the letter, but the letter showed that the teacher remembered her with pride, so the belief must come before it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Until then" shows that Oksana held this belief up to the moment she read the letter.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: By the sixteenth century, the Julian calendar, which added a leap day every four years, had drifted roughly ten days out of step with the seasons, because the true solar year is about eleven minutes shorter than the 365.25 days the calendar assumed. The reform that Pope Gregory XIII decreed in 1582 corrected the error in two ways: it removed the accumulated days at a single stroke, and it changed the leap-year rule so that the drift would not recur. ______ in Catholic countries that adopted the change at once, Thursday, October 4, was followed directly by Friday, October 15, and century years would henceforth be leap years only if divisible by 400.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The second sentence names the reform's "two ways" only in general terms. The last sentence gives the exact details of both: the ten skipped days and the new rule for century years. A transition that introduces a precise account of the previous idea is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but the details carry out the reform rather than going against it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a new point, but the last sentence explains the two corrections already mentioned rather than adding a third.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "For example" would introduce one instance, but the last sentence gives the precise details of both parts of the reform, not a sample of it. It is tempting because the sentence mentions particular dates.
explanation.D: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the last sentence states exactly how the reform removed the extra days and changed the leap-year rule.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Because Earth rotates, air moving across its surface is deflected from a straight path: to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern. A large storm is a region of low pressure toward which surrounding air flows, and north of the equator the rightward deflection of that inflowing air sets the whole system turning counterclockwise, which is why hurricanes and typhoons there spin in that direction when seen from above. ______ tropical cyclones that form south of the equator, where inflowing air is deflected to the left, rotate clockwise.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Conversely,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The text explains that air is deflected right in the north and left in the south, and that the rightward deflection makes northern storms spin counterclockwise. The last sentence describes the reverse case: leftward deflection makes southern storms spin clockwise. A transition that introduces the opposite case is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" is tempting because the same mechanism is at work, but the outcome is the reverse (left instead of right, clockwise instead of counterclockwise), so the case is opposite, not similar.
explanation.B: Correct. "Conversely" signals that the southern case reverses the northern one: leftward deflection and clockwise rotation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The clockwise spin of southern storms is not caused by the counterclockwise spin of northern ones; each results from its own hemisphere's deflection.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Southern cyclones are not an example of northern storms spinning counterclockwise; they spin the other way.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Many people picture a camel's hump as a kind of water tank that lets the animal cross deserts without drinking. ______ the hump is mostly fat. When food is scarce, a camel can break down this fat for energy, which helps it travel long distances between meals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: As a result,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Instead,

explanation.why: The first sentence describes what many people believe the hump holds: water. The next sentence gives the true answer, fat, in place of that belief. The transition must show that one idea replaces another.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching idea, but fat is different from the water people imagine.
explanation.B: Incorrect. People's belief about water does not cause the hump to be made of fat.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The hump being mostly fat is not an example of the belief that it holds water; it contradicts that belief.
explanation.D: Correct. "Instead" shows that fat, not water, is what the hump actually holds, correcting the common belief.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Ancient Egyptians made writing sheets from the papyrus plant, which grew along the Nile River. First, they cut the plant's stalks into thin strips. They laid one layer of strips side by side and placed a second layer across it at a right angle. ______ they pressed the two layers together and left them to dry into a single smooth sheet.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Even so,
choices.B: Next,
choices.C: For instance,
choices.D: In contrast,

explanation.why: The text lists the steps of making a papyrus sheet in order, starting with "First." The last sentence gives the step that comes after laying the strips: pressing and drying them. A sequence transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Even so" signals that something happens despite a problem, but no problem is mentioned.
explanation.B: Correct. "Next" shows that pressing and drying come after the strips are laid in two layers.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Pressing the layers is not an instance of laying the strips; it is the following step.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Pressing the layers does not contrast with laying them; it continues the same process.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Dmitri's grandmother could recite every poem she had learned as a girl, but she could rarely remember where she had put things. ______ last week she searched the whole apartment for her reading glasses, only to find them resting on top of her head.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The first sentence says the grandmother "could rarely remember where she had put things." The last sentence tells one specific time this happened: she hunted for glasses that were on her head. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The search for the glasses does not contrast with her poor memory for objects; it shows it. The "but" in the first sentence may make a contrast word tempting.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the search replaced something mentioned earlier, but the search is one case of the forgetfulness just described.
explanation.C: Correct. "For example" introduces one specific incident that illustrates her forgetting where she put things.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In other words" restates an idea, but the last sentence adds a particular event rather than rephrasing the general statement.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Great Rann of Kutch, in the Indian state of Gujarat, is a flat, low-lying stretch of land near the Arabian Sea. During the monsoon, shallow, salty water floods much of it. When the dry season arrives, the hot sun evaporates this water. ______ a vast white crust of salt is left behind, covering the ground as far as the eye can see.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The text explains that salty water floods the land and then evaporates in the sun. The last sentence gives what this evaporation produces: a crust of salt. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The salt crust is not an example of the water evaporating; it is what the evaporation leaves behind.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel idea, but the last sentence describes a result.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The salt crust does not contrast with the evaporation; it follows from it.
explanation.D: Correct. "As a result" shows that the salt crust is left because the salty water evaporates.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The harmonica is a popular first instrument for young musicians. It is small enough to fit in a pocket, so it can be carried and played almost anywhere. ______ it is inexpensive, and a beginner can make a pleasant sound simply by breathing in and out through its holes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In addition,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The text gives reasons the harmonica is a good first instrument. The second sentence gives one reason (it is small and easy to carry), and the last sentence gives more reasons (it is cheap and easy to play). A transition that adds another point is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "In addition" adds further reasons, low cost and easy playing, to the first reason, its small size.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Being inexpensive does not contrast with being portable; both are advantages.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Low cost is not an example of the harmonica being small; it is a separate advantage.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The harmonica's small size does not make it inexpensive or easy to play.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The ostrich, the largest living bird, has wings far too small to lift its heavy body off the ground. ______ it is hardly defenseless. Its long, powerful legs allow it to run at speeds of up to about 70 kilometers per hour, fast enough to escape many predators.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Still,
choices.C: Therefore,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The first sentence states a weakness: the ostrich cannot fly. The next sentence says that, despite this, the bird is "hardly defenseless." The transition must show that the second idea is true in spite of the first.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching idea, but the second sentence pushes against the first.
explanation.B: Correct. "Still" shows that, although the ostrich cannot fly, it is nevertheless able to protect itself.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Being unable to fly would not lead to the bird being well defended; "Therefore" sets up the wrong cause and effect.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Being "hardly defenseless" is not an example of having wings too small to fly.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The ocotillo, a spiny shrub of the deserts of northern Mexico and the southwestern United States, is described by botanists as drought deciduous. ______ it drops its small leaves whenever the soil dries out, then grows a fresh set within a few days after rain falls.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: By contrast,
choices.D: Even so,

explanation.why: The first sentence uses a technical term, "drought deciduous." The second sentence explains in plain words what the term means: the plant drops its leaves when the soil is dry. A transition that restates an idea more simply is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" compares two different things, but the second sentence explains the same idea.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" signals that the second sentence restates "drought deciduous" in everyday language.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the second sentence contrasts with the first.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Dropping leaves in dry soil does not go against being drought deciduous; it is what the term means.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The earliest Roman calendar began the year in March. Its seventh month was called September, from septem, the Latin word for "seven." Later, two months, January and February, were added, and the year eventually came to begin in January. ______ September became the ninth month, even though its name still means "seven."
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In contrast,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The text explains that two months were added and the year came to start in January. That change moved September from seventh place to ninth. The last sentence is the effect of that change, so a cause-and-effect transition is needed. (In American English the period goes inside the closing quotation mark.)
explanation.A: Incorrect. The last sentence does not oppose the earlier ones; it follows from them. The "even though" in that sentence may make a contrast word tempting.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel idea, but the last sentence states a consequence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. September becoming the ninth month is not an example of the calendar change; it is what the change caused.
explanation.D: Correct. "As a result" shows that September became the ninth month because January and February came to start the year.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Every morning in Multan, Rehana's grandmother followed the same routine. She watered the jasmine plants on the roof, swept the courtyard, and fed the sparrows that waited on the wall. ______ with her chores done, she sat by the window with a cup of tea and waited for the newspaper to arrive.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Finally,

explanation.why: The text describes the grandmother's morning routine as a series of tasks. The last sentence, "with her chores done," tells what she does at the end of that series. A sequence transition that marks the last step is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Sitting with tea is not an example of a chore; the sentence says the chores are "done."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The last sentence adds a new step rather than restating the chores.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean she sat down in place of doing the chores, but she had already done them.
explanation.D: Correct. "Finally" marks sitting with her tea as the last part of her routine, after the chores.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Many spiders that build webs have poor eyesight. They find their prey mainly by feeling the vibrations an insect makes when it gets caught in the silk. ______ jumping spiders, which do not use webs to trap prey, have sharp vision. They spot an insect from a distance, creep toward it, and then leap onto it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: Web-building spiders are described as having poor eyesight and hunting by feel. Jumping spiders are described as having sharp vision and hunting by sight. The transition must show that these two groups differ.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Web builders' poor eyesight does not cause jumping spiders to see well.
explanation.B: Correct. "In contrast" signals the difference between web builders' poor eyesight and jumping spiders' sharp vision.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a likeness, but jumping spiders see well while web builders do not.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Jumping spiders are not an example of web-building spiders with poor eyesight; they are the opposite case.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: When foods traveled from one part of the world to another, their names often traveled with them. ______ the English word "tomato" comes from tomatl, a word in Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs. The Aztecs grew tomatoes in Mexico long before Spanish traders brought the plant to Europe in the 1500s.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: However,

explanation.why: The first sentence makes a general claim: food names often moved along with the foods. The next sentence gives one case of this, the word "tomato," which came to English from Nahuatl. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "For example" introduces "tomato" as one case of a food name traveling with the food.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the tomato's name replaced the general pattern, but it fits the pattern.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The general pattern did not cause this word to come from Nahuatl; the word is one instance of the pattern.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The history of "tomato" supports the general claim instead of contrasting with it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In Tamil Nadu, in southern India, many women begin the day by drawing a kolam, a pattern of lines and loops, on the ground outside the front door. The design welcomes visitors and decorates the home's entrance. ______ because a kolam is traditionally made with rice flour, it also provides food for ants and small birds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: However,
choices.C: In addition,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second sentence gives two purposes of a kolam: welcoming visitors and decorating the entrance. The last sentence gives one more purpose, feeding ants and birds, and even uses the word "also." A transition that adds a point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The kolam feeds animals as well as decorating, not in place of decorating.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Feeding small animals does not contrast with welcoming visitors; it is another positive purpose.
explanation.C: Correct. "In addition" adds a further purpose of the kolam, matching the word "also" in the sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Feeding ants and birds is not an example of decorating the entrance; it is a separate benefit.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Most people picture medieval European castles as great fortresses of stone. ______ many of the first castles built in England after the Norman Conquest of 1066 were made of earth and timber. These motte-and-bailey castles, each a wooden tower set on a mound of earth beside a fenced yard, could be built in just a few weeks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The first sentence describes the usual image of castles: stone fortresses. The second says many early English castles were made of earth and wood instead. A transition that shows a contrast is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. People's image of stone castles did not cause early castles to be made of wood.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Wooden castles are not an example of stone fortresses; they differ from them.
explanation.C: Correct. "However" signals the contrast between the usual image of stone castles and the earth-and-timber castles described next.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a likeness, but earth and timber differ from stone.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Medieval glassmakers could not produce large, flat sheets of glass; they could make only fairly small pieces. ______ the makers of stained-glass windows built each picture from many small pieces of colored glass, joined by thin strips of lead that held them in place.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The first sentence states a limit: glassmakers could make only small pieces of glass. The second sentence explains what window makers did because of that limit: they built pictures from many small pieces. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Building windows from small pieces is not an instance of glassmakers' inability to make large sheets; it is a result of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something happens despite a problem, but using small pieces is a response to the limit, not a defiance of it.
explanation.C: Correct. "Consequently" shows that windows were made of many small pieces because large sheets could not be produced.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel fact, but the second sentence describes a consequence.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A few kinds of birds use objects as tools. ______ the Egyptian vulture, which lives in parts of Africa, Europe, and Asia, picks up stones in its beak and throws them at ostrich eggs. The shells of these eggs are too thick to break with a peck, but repeated blows from a stone eventually crack them open.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: As a result,
choices.B: Finally,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The first sentence makes a general claim: some birds use tools. The next sentence describes one bird that does so, the Egyptian vulture throwing stones. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The fact that some birds use tools does not cause the vulture to throw stones; the vulture is one case of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Finally" marks the last step or item in a series, but no series has been started.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The vulture's use of stones supports the first sentence rather than contrasting with it.
explanation.D: Correct. "For example" introduces the Egyptian vulture as one bird that uses objects as tools.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The archerfish, found in coastal waters and mangrove swamps from India to northern Australia, catches insects resting on leaves and branches above the water without ever leaving the water itself. It relies on a weapon built into its own mouth. ______ by pressing its tongue against a groove in the roof of its mouth, the fish forms a narrow tube, through which it fires a jet of water that knocks the insect down into the water.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Moreover,
choices.B: Specifically,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The second sentence mentions the archerfish's weapon only in general terms: something "built into its own mouth." The last sentence explains exactly what that weapon is and how it works, a tube formed by the tongue that shoots water. A transition that introduces a precise account of something just mentioned is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a new point, but the last sentence does not add a second fact; it explains the weapon already mentioned.
explanation.B: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the last sentence states exactly what the weapon "built into its own mouth" is.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the fish uses the water jet in place of its mouth, but the jet is made by its mouth.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The description of the water jet does not go against anything in the earlier sentences; it fills in their details.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Gerardus Mercator's world map of 1569 remains one of the most influential maps ever drawn. ______ it badly distorts the sizes of lands far from the equator: on it, Greenland appears roughly as large as Africa, which is actually about fourteen times bigger. But the map has a property that sailors valued: any course with a constant compass bearing appears on it as a straight line, so navigators could plot routes with a ruler.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Admittedly,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The text praises the map, then admits a serious weakness (it distorts sizes), and then returns with "But" to explain why the map was still valued. The blank must introduce a point the writer concedes before restating the main claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The map's influence does not cause it to distort sizes; "Consequently" sets up a false cause and effect.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Distorting sizes is not an example of the map's influence; it is a drawback that cuts against it.
explanation.C: Correct. "Admittedly" signals that the writer grants a weakness of the map before explaining, with "But," why it was still important.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the distortion is a weakness that differs from the praise before it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Mrs. Osei, who taught mathematics at the village school for thirty years, never refused her students directly. When someone asked to skip a quiz or to leave class early, she would smile, say, "We'll see," and turn back to the board. Her students soon noticed that "we'll see" never once ended in a yes. ______ the phrase was simply her polite way of saying no.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Meanwhile,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The text shows that "we'll see" was always Mrs. Osei's answer to requests she did not grant, and that it "never once ended in a yes." The last sentence states that meaning plainly: the phrase was a polite refusal. A transition that restates and sums up the earlier point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The last sentence does not give one case of the pattern; it explains what the whole pattern means.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates, in plain terms, what the students had noticed about the phrase.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Meanwhile" signals something happening at the same time, but the last sentence explains the phrase rather than describing a separate event.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the phrase being a refusal agrees with the fact that it never led to a yes.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Wind, ice, and rivers constantly wear rock away from the Himalayas, carrying huge amounts of sediment down to the plains of South Asia. One might expect this steady erosion to make the mountains slowly shrink. ______ much of the range is still rising, because the Indian tectonic plate continues to push northward into Asia, forcing rock upward faster, in many places, than erosion can remove it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second sentence sets up an expectation: erosion should make the mountains shrink. The last sentence says the opposite is true: much of the range is still rising. A transition that signals a contrast with the expectation is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Erosion would not cause the mountains to rise; the rise happens despite erosion. The "because" later in the sentence may make a cause word tempting.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals agreement, but rising contradicts the expected shrinking.
explanation.C: Correct. "However" signals that the mountains are rising, contrary to the expectation that erosion would make them shrink.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Rising mountains are not an example of the shrinking that one might expect; they go against it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: For centuries, owning a portrait meant paying a painter for many hours of work, so portraits were mostly a luxury of the wealthy. By the 1850s, however, a photographic portrait cost far less than a painted one and could be completed in a single short sitting. ______ many working- and middle-class families who had never been able to afford a painting of a relative could now own pictures of their loved ones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains that photographic portraits were cheap and quick. The last sentence describes what followed from this: families who could not afford paintings could now own portraits. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something happens despite an obstacle, but cheap photographs made owning portraits easier, not harder.
explanation.B: Correct. "Consequently" shows that more families could own portraits because photographic portraits were cheap and fast to make.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Although the families differ from the wealthy mentioned earlier, the last sentence follows from the low cost of photographs in the sentence just before it; it does not contrast with it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Families owning photographs is not an instance of photographs being cheap and quick; it is the result.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1928, the Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold growing in a dish in his London laboratory had killed the bacteria around it. Fleming named the substance the mold produced penicillin, but he was unable to extract it in amounts large enough to treat patients. ______ around 1940, a team at the University of Oxford led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain found a way to purify penicillin, and large-scale production soon followed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Later,
choices.B: Previously,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The text moves forward in time: Fleming's discovery in 1928, his failure to extract enough penicillin, and then the Oxford team's success around 1940. The blank must show that the Oxford work came after Fleming's.
explanation.A: Correct. "Later" shows that the Oxford team's success around 1940 came after Fleming's discovery in 1928.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Previously" would place the Oxford work before Fleming's, but 1940 comes after 1928.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The Oxford team's success is not an example of Fleming's difficulty; it is the next stage of the story.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The Oxford team succeeded where Fleming had failed, so its work was not similar to his.

items.subject: science
items.passage: By damming streams with branches and mud, beavers create ponds that serve them well: the deep water around their lodges, which the beavers enter through underwater tunnels, helps keep predators such as wolves away. ______ these ponds benefit many other animals, since their still, shallow edges provide habitat for fish, frogs, insects, and waterbirds that would find little shelter in a fast-flowing stream.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Even so,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The first sentence explains how the ponds help the beavers themselves. The second sentence adds a different benefit: the ponds also help many other animals. A transition that adds a further point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Even so" signals a contrast with a drawback, but helping other animals does not push against helping beavers.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds a second benefit of the ponds, to other animals, after the first benefit, to beavers.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the ponds help other animals in place of helping beavers, but the text says they help beavers too.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce details of how the ponds protect beavers, but the sentence describes a new benefit for other species.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Many English words were borrowed from South Asian languages during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, and some of them changed meaning after they arrived. ______ "shampoo" comes from the Hindi word champo, meaning "press" or "knead." When it first entered English, it referred to a massage of the head and body; only later did it come to mean soap for washing hair.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first sentence claims that some borrowed words changed meaning in English. The rest of the text gives one such word, "shampoo," which once meant a massage and now means a hair-washing soap. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "In other words" restates the same idea, but the sentence moves from a general claim to one particular word.
explanation.B: Correct. "For instance" introduces "shampoo" as one borrowed word whose meaning changed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The general pattern of borrowing did not cause "shampoo" to come from Hindi; the word is an instance of that pattern.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The history of "shampoo" supports the claim about changing meanings; it does not contrast with it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The cabin was cramped and drafty, its roof leaked whenever it rained, and the nearest town was an hour's drive down a rough dirt road. Aleksander's mother complained about it every year, and his younger sister counted the days until they could go home. ______ every summer the family returned to the cabin, and every summer Aleksander found himself sorry to leave.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Even so,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The first two sentences list the cabin's problems and the family's complaints, which would lead a reader to expect the family to stop going. The last sentence says they returned anyway, and Aleksander was sad to leave. A transition that signals something happening despite what came before is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Returning every summer is not an example of the cabin's problems or the family's complaints.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The cabin's flaws and the complaints would not cause the family to keep returning; "Consequently" reverses the logic.
explanation.C: Correct. "Even so" shows that the family kept returning despite the cabin's flaws and the complaints.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence does not restate the complaints; it tells what the family did in spite of them.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most bony fish stay afloat with a swim bladder, a gas-filled sac they can inflate or deflate to rise or sink in the water. Sharks, however, have no swim bladder and would slowly sink if they had no other way to stay up. ______ they rely partly on a large liver filled with oil, which is lighter than seawater, and partly on the lift their fins create as they swim.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: In addition,

explanation.why: The text explains that sharks lack the swim bladder that keeps most fish afloat. The last sentence tells what sharks use in place of it: an oily liver and lift from their fins. A transition that introduces a replacement or alternative is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The oily liver is not an example of sinking or of a swim bladder; it is a different way of staying afloat.
explanation.B: Correct. "Instead" shows that sharks use an oily liver and fin lift in place of the swim bladder they lack.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" would suggest sharks stay afloat the same way bony fish do, but the text says they lack a swim bladder.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In addition" would add another feature on top of a swim bladder, but sharks have no swim bladder to add to.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the third century BCE, the emperor Ashoka, who ruled much of the Indian subcontinent, had messages to his subjects carved on rocks and stone pillars across his empire. These edicts were not identical everywhere; they were adapted to the regions where they stood. ______ the edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, in present-day Pakistan, were carved in Kharosthi, a script used in the northwest, while most edicts elsewhere used the Brahmi script.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: However,

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim: the edicts were adapted to their regions. The last sentence gives one case of this, the northwestern edicts written in the local Kharosthi script. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "For instance" introduces the Kharosthi edicts as one example of how the edicts were adapted to their regions.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The Kharosthi script is not a result of the edicts being adapted; it is one of the ways they were adapted.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the general claim, but the sentence names particular sites and a particular script.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The use of Kharosthi in the northwest supports the claim that the edicts were adapted; it does not contrast with it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Unlike free verse, which has no fixed length or rhyme, a traditional sonnet follows a strict pattern. ______ an English sonnet has exactly fourteen lines: three groups of four lines with alternating rhymes, followed by a final pair of lines that rhyme with each other. Poets who choose this form must fit their ideas within these limits, often saving a surprising turn of thought for that closing pair.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first sentence says only that a sonnet "follows a strict pattern." The next sentence spells out exactly what that pattern is: fourteen lines arranged and rhymed in a set way. A transition that introduces precise details of something just mentioned is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the sentence states exactly what the sonnet's "strict pattern" is.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The contrast with free verse is already made inside the first sentence; the next sentence does not replace the sonnet's pattern with something else but explains it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a comparison with a different thing, but the sentence describes the same strict pattern in detail.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The fourteen-line pattern does not go against the idea of a strict form; it describes that form.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The flowers of some hydrangeas change color depending on the soil they grow in. In acidic soil, the plants can absorb aluminum, which turns their flowers blue. In less acidic soil, the aluminum stays locked in forms the roots cannot take up, and the flowers stay pink. ______ two plants of the same variety may bloom blue in one garden and pink in another.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: As a result,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The text explains that soil acidity controls whether hydrangeas can take up aluminum, and that aluminum makes the flowers blue. The last sentence describes what follows from this: identical plants can bloom in different colors in different soils. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel fact, but the last sentence is a consequence of how soil affects color.
explanation.B: Correct. "As a result" shows that plants of one variety can bloom in different colors because soil acidity controls their uptake of aluminum.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence does mention two colors, but it does not contrast with the explanation before it; it follows from that explanation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something surprising given what came before, but different colors in different gardens are exactly what the explanation predicts.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Much of Venice, Italy, stands on millions of wooden piles, tree trunks that builders drove deep into the muddy floor of the lagoon centuries ago. Wood that is exposed to air and moisture usually rots within a few decades. ______ many of these piles remain sound today, because the waterlogged mud around them holds so little oxygen that the fungi and bacteria that cause decay cannot thrive.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Therefore,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The second sentence says wood usually rots within decades, which would lead a reader to expect the old piles to have decayed. The last sentence says many remain sound anyway. A transition that signals something true despite what came before is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching idea, but the piles' survival is unlike the usual rotting of wood.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Sound piles are not an example of wood rotting; they are an exception to it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Wood usually rotting would not lead to the piles staying sound. The "because" later in the sentence may make a cause word tempting, but that cause is the low-oxygen mud, not the rotting.
explanation.D: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that the piles have survived despite the fact that wood usually rots.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Around 530 BCE, workers on the Greek island of Samos began cutting a tunnel more than a kilometer long through a mountain to carry water to the island's main town. One team of workers dug inward from the north side of the mountain. ______ a second team dug inward from the south side. Remarkably, the two tunnels met near the middle of the mountain, only a few meters out of line.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Afterward,
choices.B: Meanwhile,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The text describes two teams digging from opposite sides of the mountain, and their tunnels met near the middle. For the tunnels to meet in the middle, the teams must have been digging during the same period. A transition that shows actions happening at the same time is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Afterward" would mean the south team started after the north team finished, but then the tunnels could not have met near the middle.
explanation.B: Correct. "Meanwhile" shows that the second team dug from the south while the first team dug from the north.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The second team's work is not an example of the first team's digging; it is a separate, simultaneous effort.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence describes a second team, not a restatement of the first team's work.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Like most cephalopods, the common octopus has eyes containing only one type of light-sensitive pigment, an arrangement that in other animals goes along with an inability to tell colors apart. Laboratory tests have generally confirmed this expectation: octopuses trained to choose between objects that differ in color but not in brightness perform no better than chance. ______ octopuses match the colors of the reefs and seaweeds around them with striking accuracy, shifting the hue of their skin within a fraction of a second, an ability whose basis researchers are still working to explain.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first two sentences build an expectation that octopuses cannot distinguish colors, and lab tests support it. The last sentence reports something that seems to conflict with that expectation: octopuses still match colors accurately. The transition must show that this ability exists in spite of what came before, while the earlier facts remain true.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Therefore" would make accurate color matching a result of having only one pigment, which reverses the logic: one pigment would lead us to expect poor color matching.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" signals that one thing replaces another, but the color matching does not replace the single pigment or the test results; all of these facts stand together. This is the closest near miss because it also sounds like a contrast.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a point that resembles the previous one, but the color matching conflicts with the test results rather than resembling them.
explanation.D: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that octopuses match colors well despite the evidence that they cannot tell colors apart.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Many accounts portray the printing press as having made the handwritten book obsolete almost overnight. Granted, scribes did not vanish when Johannes Gutenberg's workshop in Mainz began printing in the 1450s: wealthy patrons went on commissioning illuminated manuscripts for decades, and some copyists even produced handwritten copies of printed books. ______ the overall shift was remarkably swift by the standards of the age, for by 1500 presses had been set up in well over two hundred European towns and had produced, by most estimates, millions of printed volumes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Still,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Granted,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The second sentence begins with "Granted," conceding that handwritten books lingered. The last sentence turns back to the main point: the shift to print was swift. After a concession, the writer needs a transition that returns to the main claim in spite of the point just conceded.
explanation.A: Correct. "Still" signals that, despite the conceded persistence of scribes, the overall shift to print was fast.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The spread of presses to more than two hundred towns is not an example of scribes continuing to work; it points the other way.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Granted" introduces a concession, but the last sentence is not another point against the main claim; it argues for the main claim. Using "Granted" again would mislabel it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the rapid spread of printing contrasts with the persistence of handwritten books described just before it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Sundarbans, the vast mangrove forest that spans the coasts of Bangladesh and India, takes its name, according to a common explanation, from the sundari tree, one of its most abundant species. Like other mangroves, the sundari grows in waterlogged mud that holds very little oxygen, and it copes with this problem chiefly through a single adaptation of its root system. ______ its roots send up short, peg-like projections called pneumatophores, which rise above the mud and draw in air through tiny pores on their surfaces, supplying oxygen to the buried roots below.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Likewise,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Specifically,
choices.D: Even so,

explanation.why: The second sentence says the sundari copes with low oxygen through "a single adaptation of its root system" but does not say what that adaptation is. The last sentence names and describes it. The transition must introduce a precise account of something just mentioned in general terms.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Likewise" introduces a separate but similar case, yet the last sentence describes the same tree and the same adaptation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For example" would present the pneumatophores as one case among several, but the text says the tree relies on "a single adaptation." The last sentence describes that adaptation itself rather than offering an example of it. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the last sentence states exactly what the "single adaptation of its root system" is.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Even so" signals a contrast, but the pneumatophores do not conflict with anything in the previous sentence; they explain how the tree copes.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In the painting workshop maintained by the Mughal emperor Akbar in the late sixteenth century, an illustrated manuscript page was seldom the work of a single artist from start to finish. ______ the labor was usually divided among specialists: one painter sketched the overall composition, a second applied the colors, and a third, often a celebrated portraitist, painted the faces of the principal figures. Brief notes written in the margins of many surviving pages record which artist performed each of these tasks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first sentence says what usually did not happen: one artist doing a whole page. The second sentence says what happened in its place: the work was divided among specialists. A transition that introduces an alternative to something just ruled out is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The division of labor is not a result of pages seldom being one artist's work; it is the same practice described positively.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a new point, but the second sentence does not add a separate idea; it states what replaced single-artist work.
explanation.C: Correct. "Instead" signals that dividing the labor among specialists took the place of a single artist finishing the page.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean the division of labor happened in spite of the first sentence, but the two sentences agree: a page was seldom one artist's work because the labor was shared. This is the closest near miss because it is also a contrast word.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Water fleas of the genus Daphnia often reproduce without mating, so a single female can give rise to a large clone of genetically identical offspring. When young members of some clones develop in water containing chemicals released by predatory insect larvae, they grow pointed helmets and spines that make them harder to swallow; their identical sisters raised in predator-free water grow no such defenses. ______ one set of genes can yield either a defended or an undefended body, depending on the chemical surroundings in which an individual develops.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes genetically identical sisters that grow different bodies in different water. The last sentence states the general meaning of that observation in plainer terms: the same genes can produce either body type, depending on the environment. A restatement transition fits.
explanation.A: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates the observation about identical sisters as a general point about genes and environment.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For instance" introduces an example, but the last sentence is a general statement; the specific example came in the sentence before it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the last sentence agrees with and sums up the previous sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a new case that resembles the previous one, but the last sentence describes the same water fleas, not a parallel case. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Along the road network of the Inca Empire, which stretched for more than 30,000 kilometers through the Andes, the state maintained waystations known as tambos, spaced roughly a day's walk apart, where officials, soldiers, and relay runners could find food, shelter, and stored supplies. ______ the Royal Road of the Persian Achaemenid Empire, built some two thousand years earlier, was lined with stations about a day's ride apart, at which royal messengers could rest and exchange tired horses for fresh ones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Specifically,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The first sentence describes Inca waystations placed a day's travel apart. The second describes a different empire's road with stations also placed a day's travel apart. The transition must link two separate cases that resemble each other.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The Persian road was built about two thousand years before the Inca network, so it cannot be a result of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would mean the second sentence restates the first, but it describes a different empire, a different road, and a different era. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Specifically" introduces more precise detail about the same subject, but the second sentence moves to a new subject, the Persian road.
explanation.D: Correct. "Similarly" signals that the Persian road stations resemble the Inca tambos.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Builders in late antiquity and the Middle Ages often incorporated spolia—columns, carved panels, and other pieces taken from older structures—into new monuments. Scholars once dismissed the practice as a sign of declining craftsmanship, but many now argue that reused pieces were often chosen deliberately, for the prestige of the past they carried. ______ the Arch of Constantine, completed in Rome in 315 CE, displays relief panels originally carved for monuments to Trajan, Hadrian, and Marcus Aurelius, emperors whom later Romans remembered as model rulers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Specifically,
choices.C: Accordingly,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim about many monuments: reused pieces were often chosen for the prestige they carried. The last sentence describes one particular monument whose reused panels came from admired emperors. The transition must introduce a single case that illustrates the general claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but the Arch of Constantine supports the newer view rather than challenging it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a more precise statement of the same claim, but the arch is one instance drawn from a broad practice, not a more exact version of the claim itself. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "as a result," but the arch was not built because scholars later changed their view of spolia.
explanation.D: Correct. "For example" signals that the arch is one illustration of builders reusing prestigious older pieces.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Mrs. Okonjo had always insisted that the old upright piano was not worth the space it took up in the front room, and her daughter had never quite managed to disagree. ______ its keys stuck in damp weather, its lid was scarred with rings from forgotten teacups, and two of its strings had gone unreplaced for years. But on the evenings when Tobi sat down at it after supper, picking out the hymns his grandfather used to play, even Mrs. Okonjo stopped what she was doing to listen, and no one ever mentioned selling it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Still,
choices.D: Granted,

explanation.why: The second sentence lists the piano's flaws, which support Mrs. Okonjo's complaint, and the third sentence begins "But," turning to the reason the family keeps the piano. The blank must introduce a concession: the narrator admits the flaws before arguing the other way.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The flaws are not a result of Mrs. Okonjo's opinion; if anything, they are the reason for it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" signals a replacement, but the flaws do not replace anything in the first sentence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Still" signals a contrast with what came before, but the list of flaws agrees with Mrs. Okonjo's complaint instead of contrasting with it. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Correct. "Granted" concedes the piano's flaws before the "But" sentence explains why the family keeps it anyway.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most of the sunlight that strikes a conventional dark roof is absorbed and converted to heat, which then flows into the building below and into the surrounding air. Roofs coated with pale, highly reflective materials, by contrast, send a much larger share of the incoming sunlight back toward the sky. ______ buildings with such coatings tend to stay cooler on summer afternoons, and their top floors typically require less air-conditioning, though the savings depend on the local climate and on how well the roof is insulated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nonetheless,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains that reflective roofs absorb less sunlight. The last sentence describes what follows from that: cooler buildings and less need for air-conditioning. The transition must signal an effect of the cause just described.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nonetheless" signals that something happens despite what came before, but reflecting sunlight would be expected to keep buildings cooler, not work against it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" would present the cooler buildings as a separate, additional point, but they follow directly from the reflection described before. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Correct. "Consequently" shows that cooler buildings result from roofs that reflect more sunlight.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Cooler buildings are an effect of reflective roofs, not an example of them.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Most Arabic-language newspapers and books are printed in Naskh, a script style in which the letters of each word sit along a single level baseline, an arrangement that adapted fairly easily to movable type. ______ Nastaliq, the style long favored for writing Urdu, sets each word on a diagonal that slopes downward from right to left, so that letters stack and overlap in ways that resisted mechanical typesetting; for much of the twentieth century, many Urdu newspapers were therefore written out by hand by calligraphers and reproduced by lithography.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: By contrast,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first sentence describes Naskh: level letters that suited movable type. The second describes Nastaliq: sloping, overlapping letters that resisted typesetting. The transition must set two different things side by side and show how they differ.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a likeness, but the text stresses how Nastaliq differs from Naskh.
explanation.B: Correct. "By contrast" sets Nastaliq's sloping, overlapping words against Naskh's level baseline.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nastaliq's diagonal form is not caused by Naskh's suitability for movable type.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something holds true in spite of what came before, but Nastaliq's slope is not a surprising outcome of Naskh's level baseline. The two scripts are simply being compared. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: English is the dominant spoken language of both the United States and the United Kingdom, yet American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) are largely unintelligible to each other's users: they differ in vocabulary, in grammar, and even in the manual alphabet used to spell out words. ASL is closely related to French Sign Language, a link that dates to 1817, when a Deaf teacher from France helped found the first permanent school for Deaf students in the United States. ______ the history of a sign language need not follow the history of the spoken language used around it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Thus,
choices.B: Nonetheless,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The first two sentences give evidence: ASL and BSL differ even though both countries speak English, and ASL descends instead from French Sign Language. The last sentence draws a general conclusion from that evidence. The transition must signal a conclusion.
explanation.A: Correct. "Thus" signals that the last sentence is the conclusion the evidence about ASL and BSL supports.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Nonetheless" signals a contrast, but the conclusion agrees with the evidence before it. This is a tempting choice because the first sentence contains a contrast ("yet"), but that contrast is already resolved.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" introduces a similar, separate point, but the last sentence is the conclusion drawn from the ASL and BSL facts, not another case like them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence is a general claim, not a specific example; the examples came earlier.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Under the Montreal Protocol, signed in 1987, nations agreed to phase out chlorofluorocarbons and other chemicals that destroy ozone in the upper atmosphere. The agreement is widely regarded as a success: atmospheric concentrations of these chemicals have been declining, and satellite measurements indicate that the seasonal ozone hole over Antarctica has begun, unevenly, to shrink. ______ because the chemicals persist in the atmosphere for decades, current projections do not place the Antarctic ozone layer's return to its 1980 condition until around the 2060s.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: Even so,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: Accordingly,

explanation.why: The second sentence presents the protocol's success. The last sentence adds a limitation that coexists with that success: full recovery is still decades away. The transition must introduce a qualification without denying the success.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the slow recovery replaces the success, but the text says both are true. This is the closest near miss because it also signals a contrast.
explanation.B: Correct. "Even so" signals that, despite the encouraging signs, recovery will take decades.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence adds new information about the timeline; it does not restate the protocol's success.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "as a result," but a slow recovery is not a result of the protocol's success; it is caused by how long the chemicals persist.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Between 1405 and 1433, fleets commanded by the Chinese admiral Zheng He made seven voyages across the Indian Ocean, some with more than a hundred ships, reaching ports in Southeast Asia, India, Arabia, and East Africa. ______ Portuguese sailors were making their first cautious ventures into the open Atlantic, reaching the island of Madeira around 1420 and the Azores by the end of that decade, though decades more would pass before a Portuguese ship rounded the southern tip of Africa.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Meanwhile,
choices.C: Subsequently,
choices.D: Therefore,

explanation.why: The first sentence covers 1405 to 1433. The second describes Portuguese voyages around 1420 and later that decade, which fall inside that same span. The transition must show that the two sets of events happened at the same time.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The Portuguese voyages are not an example of Zheng He's voyages; they were made by a different people.
explanation.B: Correct. "Meanwhile" signals that the Portuguese voyages took place during the same years as Zheng He's.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Subsequently" means "afterward," but the Portuguese reached Madeira around 1420, while Zheng He's voyages were still under way. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The Portuguese voyages were not a result of Zheng He's voyages; the text links them only in time.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Acousticians describe a room's reverberation time as the number of seconds a sound takes to fade by sixty decibels after its source stops. A long reverberation time, around two seconds or more, lets the notes of choral or organ music blend into a rich, continuous sound, which is one reason many large stone churches are prized as venues for such music. ______ a short reverberation time, closer to one second, suits speech and drama, since each syllable fades before the next one can blur it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Conversely,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The second sentence says a long reverberation time suits blended music. The last sentence states the reverse case: a short reverberation time suits speech. The transition must introduce the opposite side of the same relationship.
explanation.A: Correct. "Conversely" signals that the last sentence reverses the previous case: short instead of long, speech instead of choral music.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something is true in spite of what came before, but short reverberation suiting speech does not go against long reverberation suiting choral music. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A short reverberation time for speech is not an example of a long reverberation time suiting music.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but the last sentence describes the opposite case, not a matching one.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The platypus departs from the usual pattern of mammalian life in several ways. Females lay leathery eggs rather than giving birth to live young, and after the eggs hatch, they feed their young on milk that seeps from patches of skin on the belly, since they have no nipples. ______ adult males are among the very few venomous mammals: each carries a sharp spur on the ankle of each hind leg that can deliver venom strong enough to disable a small animal and to cause intense, lasting pain in humans.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Consequently,
