explanation.why: The first sentence says the platypus is unusual "in several ways." The second sentence gives the first set of ways (egg laying and milk without nipples). The last sentence adds a further, separate way: males are venomous. The transition must add another point in support of the same claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a more detailed account of the previous sentence, but venom has nothing to do with eggs or milk. It is a separate example of how the platypus is unusual. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds venom as one more way in which the platypus differs from most mammals.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but being venomous is another unusual trait, which supports the first sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Males are not venomous because females lay eggs; the two traits are independent.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most biologists do not classify viruses as living organisms, chiefly because a virus cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism on its own: outside a host cell, it is an inert package of genetic material wrapped in protein. The discovery in 2003 of mimivirus, a virus larger than some bacteria, prompted renewed debate, but it has not overturned this view. ______ mimivirus and the other giant viruses identified since then carry genes for some of the molecular machinery that cells use to build proteins, machinery that ordinary viruses lack. Yet none of these viruses possesses ribosomes, the structures in which proteins are actually assembled, so even the largest of them remain wholly dependent on the cells they infect.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Indeed,
choices.D: Granted,

explanation.why: The author's position is that giant viruses have not overturned the view that viruses are not alive. The sentence with the blank states a fact that seems to favor the other side (the genes for protein-building machinery), and the next sentence begins "Yet," returning to the author's position. The blank must introduce a concession.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The genes are not an example of the view remaining intact; they are evidence that seems to challenge it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The genes are not a result of the view surviving; they are what made the debate arise.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Indeed" would strengthen the preceding claim that the view has not been overturned, but the genes for protein-building machinery point the other way. This is the most tempting choice because it would fit if the passage stopped after "prompted renewed debate."
explanation.D: Correct. "Granted" concedes a point in favor of the opposing view before "Yet" explains why that point is not decisive.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the early nineteenth century, the mills of Dundee, Scotland, spun mainly flax, much of it imported from Russia, although a few had begun experimenting with jute, a coarse fiber grown chiefly in Bengal that was cheaper than flax but harder to spin. When the Crimean War broke out in 1853, eventually setting Britain and Russia on opposing sides, the supply of Russian flax to British mills was disrupted. ______ Dundee's manufacturers turned to jute on a far larger scale, and within a few decades the city had become so closely identified with the fiber that it was nicknamed "Juteopolis."
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes a cause: the war cut off Russian flax. The last sentence describes what the mills did in response: they shifted to jute on a large scale. The transition must signal a result.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean the mills turned to jute in spite of the flax shortage, but the shortage is the reason they turned to jute. This choice can tempt a reader who recalls that jute was "harder to spin," but that detail is not what the blank responds to.
explanation.B: Correct. "Consequently" shows that the large-scale turn to jute followed from the loss of Russian flax.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence reports a new development, not a restatement of the flax shortage.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The shift to jute is a response to the flax shortage, not an example of it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Designers of traditional Japanese gardens have long used a technique called shakkei, often translated as "borrowed scenery." In a garden built on this principle, a distant mountain, a temple roof, or a stand of trees beyond the property is not merely visible from within; it is deliberately framed by hedges, walls, and carefully placed plantings that conceal whatever lies in between, so that the remote view seems to continue the foreground without interruption. ______ the landscape beyond the garden's boundary is treated as one of the garden's own elements, even though the designer neither owns nor controls it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: By contrast,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains in detail how a shakkei garden frames a distant view so that it seems part of the garden. The last sentence sums up that same idea in plainer terms: the outside landscape becomes one of the garden's elements, which is what "borrowed scenery" means. A restatement transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The last sentence is a general summary of the technique, not a particular example of it; the examples (a mountain, a temple roof, trees) came earlier.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates what borrowing scenery amounts to.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a separate case that resembles the first, but the last sentence describes the same technique, not a parallel one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "By contrast" signals a difference, but the last sentence agrees with and summarizes the previous one. It may tempt readers who notice the phrase "neither owns nor controls," but that phrase is part of the same idea, not a contrast with the sentence before.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Eleanor had rehearsed, through the whole of the long drive from the station, the speech in which she would tell her aunt that she had accepted the teaching position in Chicago; she had polished its apologies and anticipated its objections until it seemed to her very nearly unanswerable. But when the carriage drew up and she saw the old woman waiting on the step, a shawl pulled tight against the wind and one thin hand raised in greeting, the speech deserted her entirely. ______ she heard herself asking after the roses, and the new cook, and the health of the minister's wife, as though she had come home to stay.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The second sentence says Eleanor's prepared speech "deserted her," so she does not give it. The last sentence describes what she says in its place: small talk about roses, the cook, and a neighbor. The transition must introduce what happened in place of the speech.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" signals that the small talk took the place of the speech Eleanor had planned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a further point of the same kind, but the small talk is not an addition to the speech; the speech never happens.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but asking about roses is not similar to forgetting a speech.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Eleanor made small talk in spite of losing her speech, but losing the speech does not work against small talk; the small talk fills the gap the speech left. This is the most tempting choice because the passage is full of contrast.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Collisions with the rotating blades of wind turbines kill a considerable number of birds each year, particularly large raptors such as eagles. At a wind farm on the Norwegian island of Smøla, researchers tested a simple remedy: on four turbines, they painted one of the three blades black, a change thought to reduce the motion blur that may make spinning blades hard for birds to see. Over the following years, recorded bird deaths at the painted turbines fell by roughly 70 percent compared with nearby unpainted ones. ______ the study involved only a handful of turbines at a single site, and its authors have called for larger trials before the method is widely adopted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: However,

explanation.why: The third sentence reports an encouraging result. The last sentence points out a limitation of that result: the study was small and limited to one site. The transition must introduce a qualification that contrasts with the encouraging finding without denying it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a precise detail about the 70 percent drop, but the last sentence shifts to the study's limits.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" would add another point in favor of the method, but the small size of the study is a reason for caution, not further support. This is the most tempting choice because the sentence does add information.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the small size of the study replaces the result, but the result still stands; it is only limited.
explanation.D: Correct. "However" signals that the promising result comes with an important limitation.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Historians once traced the spread of papermaking from China to the Islamic world to a single dramatic episode. According to this account, Chinese prisoners captured at the Battle of Talas in 751 taught the craft to their captors in Samarkand, from which it soon reached Baghdad and, centuries later, Europe. Many scholars now regard the story with skepticism, observing that it appears only in sources written long after the battle and that paper seems to have been known in Central Asia well before 751. ______ they propose that the technique traveled westward gradually, carried along trade routes by merchants and artisans over generations rather than introduced in a single stroke.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The third sentence says scholars doubt the single-episode story. The last sentence gives the account these scholars put in its place: a gradual spread along trade routes. The transition must introduce an alternative to an idea just rejected.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" signals that the gradual-spread account replaces the doubted single-episode story.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The gradual-spread account is not an example of the scholars' skepticism; it is their alternative explanation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean scholars propose a gradual spread in spite of their skepticism, but their skepticism is exactly what leads them to the new account. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the new account differs from the old story rather than resembling it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Painters have traditionally mixed their colors on a palette before applying them, but Georges Seurat, working in Paris in the 1880s, sought to let the viewer's eye do much of that mixing instead. ______ he applied small, separate dots of comparatively unmixed color side by side, so that, seen from a suitable distance, neighboring dots would merge in perception rather than on the canvas. Seurat believed, drawing on the color science of his day, that such optical mixing would produce more luminous effects than pigments blended beforehand, though critics have since debated whether his technique achieves that aim.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The first sentence states Seurat's general aim: to let the viewer's eye do the mixing. The second sentence explains exactly how he pursued that aim, with separate dots that merge at a distance. The transition must introduce a precise description of the method just mentioned in general terms.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a separate but parallel idea, yet the second sentence explains the same idea in detail.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For example" would present the dots as one instance among several ways Seurat let the eye mix color, but the sentence describes his method itself, not one case of it. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the dot technique carries out Seurat's aim rather than working against it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the second sentence spells out exactly how Seurat let the viewer's eye mix colors.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Convergent evolution, the independent appearance of similar traits in lineages that are not closely related, has usually been documented in anatomy: the wings of bats and birds, for instance, or the streamlined bodies of sharks and dolphins. Researchers comparing genetic sequences have now identified a number of cases in which convergence extends to the level of individual molecules. ______ echolocating bats and toothed whales, two groups whose common ancestor could not echolocate, share several of the same amino acid changes in prestin, a protein in the inner ear involved in hearing high-frequency sounds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Accordingly,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The second sentence says researchers have found "a number of cases" of molecular convergence. The last sentence describes one such case: matching changes in prestin in bats and toothed whales. The transition must introduce one instance of a general claim about several cases.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the prestin case supports the claim about molecular convergence.
explanation.B: Correct. "For example" signals that the prestin case is one of the "number of cases" just mentioned.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The shared prestin changes are not a result of researchers comparing sequences; the comparison revealed them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would present the bat and whale case as a more precise statement of the whole claim, but the claim covers "a number of cases," and this is only one of them. This is the most attractive near miss.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: A widely repeated story holds that medieval Europeans believed the Earth to be flat until explorers such as Columbus proved otherwise. Historians of science have found little support for it. Granted, a few early Christian writers, most notably Lactantius in the early fourth century, did reject the idea of a spherical Earth, and popular images of the world were not always consistent. ______ the Earth's roundness was taken for granted by most educated people throughout the Middle Ages: it was assumed in the writings of the English scholar Bede in the eighth century and taught in universities from the thirteenth century onward through astronomy textbooks such as Sacrobosco's On the Sphere.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: Still,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The third sentence begins "Granted," conceding some evidence that seems to favor the flat-Earth story. The last sentence returns to the author's main point: educated medieval people assumed a round Earth. The transition must signal a return to the main claim despite the concession.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the concession, but the last sentence says nearly the opposite. It may tempt readers who connect it to the second sentence, but the concession comes in between.
explanation.B: Correct. "Still" signals that, despite the conceded exceptions, a round Earth was the standard educated view.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Moreover" would add a point in the same direction as the sentence before, but the last sentence pushes against the concession about Lactantius instead of extending it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Medieval belief in a round Earth is not a result of a few writers rejecting the idea; it holds despite them.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In nineteenth-century Delhi, Persian remained the prestigious language of literary prose, and letters written in it customarily opened with long strings of ornate salutations and elaborate praise of the recipient. The poet Mirza Ghalib, who regarded his Persian verse as his most serious work, nonetheless wrote many of his later letters to friends in Urdu, the everyday language of the city. ______ he largely abandoned the customary openings, often greeting a friend simply by name and moving straight to news, complaints, and jokes, so that his letters read less like formal compositions than like conversations on paper.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The text describes two ways Ghalib's letters broke with custom. The second sentence gives the first: he wrote in Urdu rather than Persian. The last sentence adds a second, separate break: he dropped the ornate openings. The transition must add a further point of the same kind.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would present the dropped openings as a detailed account of writing in Urdu, but choosing a language and choosing a style of greeting are separate decisions. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds Ghalib's abandonment of ornate openings as a second departure from custom.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but dropping the ornate openings goes in the same direction as writing in everyday Urdu.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Abandoning the openings is not an example of writing in Urdu; one could write in Urdu and still use ornate openings.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Air bubbles sealed in polar ice preserve samples of the ancient atmosphere, and cores drilled at Dome C in Antarctica hold a record reaching back roughly 800,000 years. The way bubbles form complicates that record. Fresh snow is slowly compressed into firn and then into ice, and its pores stay open to the air above until they close off at depth, a process that can take centuries or even millennia. The gas in a bubble is therefore younger than the ice around it. ______ before researchers can compare past carbon dioxide levels with temperatures inferred from the ice itself, they must estimate this age difference, which at a cold, dry site such as Dome C can reach several thousand years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Accordingly,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The fourth sentence establishes that the gas in a bubble is younger than the surrounding ice. The last sentence states what researchers must do because of that fact: estimate the age difference before comparing records. The transition must signal that the last sentence follows from the one before it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but needing to estimate the age gap follows from the gap rather than contrasting with it. It may tempt a reader who notices that the passage describes a complication.
explanation.B: Correct. "Accordingly" signals that researchers must estimate the age difference because the gas is younger than the ice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a parallel case, but the last sentence describes a consequence of the same fact, not a similar fact.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a precise detail about how the gas is younger, but the last sentence moves on to what researchers must do about it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: For thirty years Nasreen's grandmother in Hyderabad had cooked the family's Eid nihari without a written recipe, measuring the spices by the cupped palm of her hand and judging the broth by its smell. Nasreen had watched her do it every year and had, at last, copied down every step in a notebook, with the quantities converted into teaspoons and minutes. ______ when she stood alone at the stove on her first Eid in Lahore, the notebook propped against the spice tin, the dish came out tasting faintly wrong, and she could not have said which of the hundred small judgments she had failed to make.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Even so,
choices.C: Accordingly,
choices.D: Instead,

explanation.why: The second sentence suggests Nasreen should succeed: she watched for years and wrote down every step. The last sentence reports that the dish still came out wrong. The transition must signal an outcome that goes against what the earlier preparation would lead a reader to expect.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but the failed dish contrasts with Nasreen's careful preparation.
explanation.B: Correct. "Even so" signals that the dish went wrong despite Nasreen's careful notes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "as a result," but careful notes would lead us to expect success, not a dish that tastes wrong.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the failed dish replaced something mentioned before, but Nasreen's notes and her cooking are not alternatives; she uses the notebook while she cooks. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: When employees must actively sign up for a workplace retirement savings plan, participation is often modest; in studies of US firms, a third or more of eligible workers have commonly failed to enroll. When the same kind of plan instead enrolls workers automatically, leaving them free to opt out at any time, participation frequently rises above 85 percent. Nothing else need differ between the two arrangements: the contribution options, the employer's matching funds, and the freedom to join or leave can be identical. ______ the large gap in participation must be attributed to the default itself, that is, to which outcome occurs for employees who never make an active choice.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Likewise,
choices.B: However,
choices.C: Thus,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The text establishes two premises: participation differs sharply between the two arrangements, and nothing but the default differs between them. The last sentence draws the conclusion these premises support: the default must explain the gap. A transition that signals a conclusion is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Likewise" introduces a similar point, but the last sentence is a conclusion drawn from the previous points, not another point of the same kind.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "However" would signal that the last sentence contrasts with the one before it, but the conclusion depends on the identical incentives rather than conflicting with them. It is tempting because the passage contrasts two participation rates, but that contrast comes earlier.
explanation.C: Correct. "Thus" signals that the last sentence is the conclusion that follows from the two premises.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence is a conclusion about all such plans, not an example of identical incentives.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: John Cage's 4′33″ (1952) instructs its performers to make no intentional sound for the work's duration of four minutes and thirty-three seconds, and audiences have sometimes received it as a provocation or a joke. Cage had come to believe that true silence does not exist, a conviction strengthened by a visit to a soundproof chamber in which he still heard sounds that he attributed to his own body. He therefore rejected the idea that the piece consists of silence. ______ he intended the work to turn listeners' attention to the sounds that are always present, such as rustling programs, distant traffic, and the breathing of the audience, and to invite them to hear those sounds as music.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Rather,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The third sentence says Cage rejected one description of the piece: that it consists of silence. The last sentence gives the description he accepted in its place: the piece directs attention to ever-present sounds. The transition must introduce a correction that replaces a rejected idea.
explanation.A: Incorrect. What Cage intended is not an example of his rejecting the idea of silence; it is the view he held instead.
explanation.B: Correct. "Rather" signals that the last sentence states what the piece is in place of what Cage said it is not.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Cage intended the work to highlight ambient sound in spite of rejecting the idea of silence, but that rejection is exactly why he saw the piece this way. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a parallel idea, but the last sentence states Cage's alternative view rather than a view like the one he rejected.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In an experiment begun in 1963 on a rocky shore in Washington State, the ecologist Robert Paine repeatedly removed the predatory sea star Pisaster ochraceus from one stretch of shoreline while leaving a neighboring stretch untouched. Without the sea stars to eat them, mussels spread across the rock and crowded out many other species, and the number of species in the experimental area fell sharply. ______ after wolves were eliminated from Yellowstone National Park in the early twentieth century, elk populations grew and, according to many ecologists, browsed streamside willows and aspens so heavily that the habitats those trees supported declined.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: For instance,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe one case: removing a predator let its prey spread and harmed many other species. The last sentence describes a different place and predator with the same pattern. The transition must link two separate cases that resemble each other.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the Yellowstone case matches the sea star case instead of contrasting with it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would mean the Yellowstone sentence restates the sea star finding, but it describes a different ecosystem, predator, and time. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "For instance" would make Yellowstone an example of Paine's experiment, but the passage makes no general claim for it to illustrate; it describes one specific experiment, and Yellowstone is a separate, parallel case.
explanation.D: Correct. "Similarly" signals that losing wolves in Yellowstone had an effect like that of removing sea stars from the shore.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Tardigrades, tiny animals usually less than a millimeter long, can survive conditions that would kill most living things. When their surroundings dry out, they pull in their legs, lose almost all of their body water, and enter a state in which their metabolism nearly stops. They can remain in this ______ condition for years and then become active again within hours of being placed in water.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: crowded
choices.B: dormant
choices.C: fragile
choices.D: familiar

explanation.why: The text says the tardigrades' metabolism "nearly stops" and that they later "become active again." The blank must describe a condition of being temporarily inactive, which is what "dormant" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about tardigrades being packed closely together.
explanation.B: Correct. A dormant state is an inactive one that can end, which matches a metabolism that "nearly stops" until the animal becomes "active again."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text stresses how tough tardigrades are: they "survive conditions that would kill most living things." Calling the condition fragile reverses that point.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says the condition is well known or familiar; the word does not describe what happens to the animal.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Farmers in low-lying parts of southern Bangladesh have long built floating gardens: thick rafts of water hyacinth and other plants, topped with soil, on which vegetables can be grown. When monsoon floods cover the fields for months, the rafts simply rise with the water. Because the gardens keep producing food through the flood season, they make farming in these areas far less ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: productive
choices.B: crowded
choices.C: uncertain
choices.D: colorful

explanation.why: The text says the gardens "keep producing food through the flood season," so farmers can count on a harvest even when their fields are underwater. A dependable harvest makes farming less unpredictable, so the blank needs a word like "uncertain."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Gardens that keep producing food during floods make farming more productive, not less.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how many people farm in these areas.
explanation.C: Correct. Because the rafts rise with the floodwater and keep producing food, farmers no longer have to wonder whether a flood will wipe out their crops, so farming becomes less uncertain.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text is about growing food during floods, not about color or appearance.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Marine biologist Ayesha Rahman expected the coral fragments transplanted onto the damaged reef to struggle in the warming water. Instead, within a single season the fragments ______ the surrounding rock, spreading so quickly that her team had to revise its growth models.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: colonized
choices.B: avoided
choices.C: resembled
choices.D: predicted

explanation.why: "Instead" tells you the fragments did the opposite of struggling, and the rest of the sentence says they were "spreading so quickly." The blank needs a verb meaning that the fragments grew over and occupied the rock, which is what "colonized" means.
explanation.A: Correct. To colonize a surface is to spread over it and settle there, which matches "spreading so quickly."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Avoiding the rock is the opposite of spreading across it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about the fragments looking like the rock.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Coral cannot predict anything; the word does not fit the sentence's meaning.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: At the family bakery, Tomasz had always been the one who rushed: he slid trays into the oven before it was fully hot and pulled loaves out the moment their crusts browned. His grandmother worked differently. She would press a thumb into the dough, wait, press again, and shape it only when it sprang back slowly. Watching her one winter morning, Tomasz finally understood that her method was not slowness for its own sake but a kind of ______ attention that the bread itself seemed to reward.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: hesitant
choices.B: careless
choices.C: impatient
choices.D: deliberate

explanation.why: The grandmother tests the dough again and again before acting, and Tomasz realizes her way of working is "not slowness for its own sake." The blank must describe careful, purposeful attention, which is what "deliberate" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Hesitant" suggests uncertainty or reluctance, but the grandmother is not unsure; her slowness has a purpose.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Testing the dough repeatedly is the opposite of careless.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Impatience describes Tomasz, who "rushed," not his grandmother.
explanation.D: Correct. "Deliberate" means careful and done on purpose, which fits a method that is "not slowness for its own sake."

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: For decades, scholars attributed every miniature in the Bellcourt Hours, a fifteenth-century prayer book, to a single illuminator. Art historian Inês Carvalho has complicated that view. Examining the paintings under magnification, she found that the faces were made with consistent fine strokes, while the decorated borders vary widely in technique. The master, she argues, painted the figures and left the margins to several assistants. Her conclusion does not ______ the traditional attribution entirely, since the most admired portions of the book remain the master's, but it does require scholars to describe the manuscript as a workshop product.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: overturn
choices.B: corroborate
choices.C: anticipate
choices.D: embellish

explanation.why: The sentence says the old view survives in part ("the most admired portions of the book remain the master's") but must still change ("but it does require scholars to describe the manuscript as a workshop product"). The blank must mean "reverse or knock down," so that the old view is not knocked down entirely but is still revised.
explanation.A: Correct. Carvalho's finding does not overturn the single-artist attribution entirely, because the master still made the most admired paintings, but it does change how the book must be described.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Corroborate" means confirm. The reason after "since" (part of the old view survives) explains why the view is not fully overturned, not why it is not fully confirmed, and the contrast "but it does require" would make no sense.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Anticipate" means foresee; a later conclusion cannot anticipate an older attribution.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Embellish" means decorate or add details; the sentence is about whether the old view survives, not about decorating it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Popular accounts often describe forests as cooperative communities in which trees use underground fungal networks to share nutrients and send warnings to their neighbors. Some ecologists consider such descriptions ______. Although fungi clearly do link the roots of many trees, these researchers note, field studies showing that resources travel between trees through those links in amounts large enough to matter are few, and their results are open to other interpretations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: baseless
choices.B: indisputable
choices.C: overstated
choices.D: obsolete

explanation.why: The ecologists accept part of the popular picture ("fungi clearly do link the roots of many trees") but say the evidence for the bigger claim, that useful amounts of resources move between trees, is thin. The blank needs a word meaning "exaggerated," not "completely wrong."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Baseless" means having no basis at all, but the researchers grant that the fungal links are real. This choice goes further than they do.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The researchers doubt the descriptions, so "indisputable" reverses their view.
explanation.C: Correct. "Overstated" means claiming more than the evidence shows, which matches researchers who accept the links but question the large transfers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Obsolete" means replaced by something newer; the text does not say a newer view has replaced the popular one.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The Greek historian Herodotus records that around 600 BCE, Phoenician sailors sent by the Egyptian king Necho II sailed all the way around Africa, a voyage said to have taken nearly three years. No physical trace of the expedition survives, and Herodotus himself rejected one detail of the sailors' report: that while sailing west around the southern end of the continent, they had the sun on their right, to the north. Yet that very detail, which the sailors had no reason to invent, is exactly what travelers south of the equator observe, and it has led many historians to regard the account as ______: not proven, certainly, but not to be dismissed as fable.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: apocryphal
choices.B: tenable
choices.C: conclusive
choices.D: credulous

explanation.why: The colon introduces a definition of the blank: the account is "not proven" but "not to be dismissed as fable." The word must describe a claim that is reasonable to hold even though it is unproven, which is what "tenable" means. The detail Herodotus doubted is what makes historians take the story seriously.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Apocryphal" means of doubtful authenticity, like a fable, which is exactly what the text says the account should not be dismissed as.
explanation.B: Correct. A tenable claim is one that can reasonably be defended, which fits an account that is unproven but supported by a convincing detail.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Conclusive" means settled beyond doubt, but the text says the account is "not proven" and no physical trace survives.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Credulous" describes a person who believes things too easily; it cannot describe an account. It may be confused with "credible."

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Newcomers to Hindustani classical music are often told that a raga is a kind of scale, but the comparison misleads. A raga specifies not only which notes may be played but how each is to be approached: some only while ascending, some only with ornament, some dwelt upon and others barely touched. In her study of concert life in Lahore, musicologist Fatima Rizvi observes that a performer is therefore never free simply to wander among the permitted notes; her improvisation, however inventive, is ______ by a grammar so detailed that trained listeners can name a raga from a few phrases.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: liberated
choices.B: enriched
choices.C: obscured
choices.D: circumscribed

explanation.why: The text says a performer is "never free simply to wander," so the blank must express a limit placed on improvisation. But "however inventive" shows that the performer still invents within those limits. The word must mean "kept within bounds," not "fully determined."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Liberated" means set free, the opposite of a performer who is "never free simply to wander."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A detailed grammar might be said to enrich music, but the sentence is about limits: the performer is "never free simply to wander," so the blank needs a word of restriction, not enhancement.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing suggests the grammar hides the improvisation; trained listeners can recognize the raga from it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Circumscribed" means restricted within limits, which fits improvisation that is inventive yet bounded by the raga's detailed rules.

items.subject: science
items.passage: When a predator comes too close, a pufferfish has a surprising defense. The fish rapidly gulps water into an unusually ______ stomach, which can swell until the pufferfish is several times its normal size. A hunter that expected an easy meal suddenly faces a round ball, often covered in spines, that is far too large to swallow.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: elastic
choices.B: empty
choices.C: delicate
choices.D: rigid

explanation.why: The stomach "can swell until the pufferfish is several times its normal size." Only a stomach that stretches a great deal could do that, so the blank needs a word meaning "stretchy," such as "elastic."
explanation.A: Correct. An elastic stomach stretches easily, which is exactly what lets it "swell" to several times the fish's normal size.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The fish fills the stomach with water; describing it as empty does not explain how it can swell so much.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the stomach is fragile; it must be tough and stretchy to hold that much water.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A rigid stomach would not stretch at all, the opposite of one that can swell to several times its size.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Field hockey at the Olympic Games was long dominated by a single team. India won the gold medal at every Olympics from 1928 through 1956, and its run of six straight titles remained ______ until the 1960 Games in Rome. There, Pakistan defeated India 1–0 in the final to win its first Olympic gold medal in the sport.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: uncertain
choices.B: unpopular
choices.C: unnoticed
choices.D: unbroken

explanation.why: The text says India won "every" Olympic gold from 1928 through 1956 and that the run lasted "until" Pakistan beat India in 1960. A streak that continues without a single loss until a certain point is one that has not been broken, so "unbroken" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. India's six titles had already been won, so there was nothing uncertain about them; the word does not describe a winning streak that simply continued.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how people felt about India's victories.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A team that "dominated" the Olympics for decades would hardly go unnoticed, and the text says nothing about people failing to notice the streak.
explanation.D: Correct. India won six titles in a row with no break, and the streak lasted until Pakistan's victory in 1960, so it remained unbroken until then.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Pavel had come to help his grandmother with her shopping, but Olga Petrovna would not hear of it. When he reached for the heaviest bag, she pulled it away, tucked it under her arm, and marched up the four flights of stairs ahead of him. At the top, she did not even stop to rest. Pavel only sighed. At eighty-one, his grandmother was as fiercely ______ as ever.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: independent
choices.B: absentminded
choices.C: generous
choices.D: timid

explanation.why: Olga "would not hear of" being helped: she pulls the bag away from Pavel and carries it up four flights herself. Someone who insists on doing things without help is independent, so "independent" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Olga refuses help and carries the heaviest bag herself, so she is fiercely independent, meaning she insists on doing things on her own.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text shows Olga being forgetful or distracted; the scene is about her refusing help.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Olga is not giving anything to anyone. She refuses Pavel's help, which shows self-reliance, not generosity.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Grabbing the bag and marching up the stairs ahead of Pavel is bold behavior, the opposite of timid.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In Java, Indonesia, puppeteers perform wayang kulit, shadow plays that can last through an entire night. The flat puppets are cut from buffalo hide, and craftspeople punch hundreds of tiny holes into each one. When a lamp shines from behind a figure, its shadow on the cloth screen is therefore not a plain dark shape but a ______ pattern of light and dark.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: frightening
choices.B: detailed
choices.C: faded
choices.D: simple

explanation.why: The puppets have "hundreds of tiny holes," and the text contrasts the result with "a plain dark shape." Light shining through so many small holes makes a pattern with many fine parts, so the blank needs a word like "detailed."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not describe how the shadows make the audience feel.
explanation.B: Correct. Hundreds of tiny holes let light through in many small spots, producing a detailed pattern rather than "a plain dark shape."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing suggests the shadow is weak or unclear; the text is about how the holes add light within the shape.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the shadow is "not a plain dark shape," so a simple pattern is the opposite of what the holes create.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The saguaro, a giant cactus of the Sonoran Desert, may go months without rain. Its thick stem is lined with deep folds, or pleats, that run from top to bottom. After a heavy storm, the cactus soaks up water quickly, and the pleats ______ like an accordion to make room for it. During long dry spells, as the plant uses up its stored water, they slowly draw back together.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: discolor
choices.B: harden
choices.C: expand
choices.D: shrink

explanation.why: The pleats change "to make room" for the water the cactus soaks up, and the last sentence says that in dry spells they "draw back together." So after rain they must do the opposite and open outward, like an accordion being stretched. "Expand" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text is about the cactus's size and shape, not its color.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text says the pleats become stiff, and hardening would not make room for water.
explanation.C: Correct. To make room for the new water, the folds spread outward, or expand, and later "draw back together" when the water is used up.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Shrinking is what happens "during long dry spells," not after a heavy storm, when the cactus needs more room.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Before the Erie Canal opened in 1825, moving a ton of flour or grain overland from Buffalo to New York City cost roughly $100. Once the canal linked Lake Erie to the Hudson River, horse-drawn boats could carry the same load for about $10. By making shipping so much cheaper, the canal greatly ______ trade between the Great Lakes region and the Atlantic coast.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: imitated
choices.B: expanded
choices.C: concealed
choices.D: delayed

explanation.why: The cost of shipping a ton of goods fell from about $100 to about $10. When moving goods becomes that much cheaper, people ship more of them, so the canal increased trade. "Expanded" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A canal cannot imitate trade, and nothing in the text is about copying anything.
explanation.B: Correct. Shipping became about ten times cheaper, so trade between the regions grew, or expanded.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about trade being hidden; it is about trade becoming cheaper.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Cheaper shipping would speed trade up and make it grow, not hold it back.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: For weeks, Bilal had practiced his speech for the school assembly in Multan, reciting it to his mirror, his little sister, and even the family's goat. His teacher, Mrs. Qureshi, had warned him that nerves often made students forget their lines. But when Bilal stepped up to the microphone, every word came out clearly and in the right order. Afterward, Mrs. Qureshi shook his hand, plainly ______ by how well he had done.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: bewildered
choices.B: impressed
choices.C: bored
choices.D: annoyed

explanation.why: Mrs. Qureshi expected nerves might make Bilal forget his lines, but "every word came out clearly." She then shakes his hand, a sign of congratulation. The blank describes her reaction to "how well he had done," so a word showing admiration, such as "impressed," fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Shaking his hand is a sign of approval; the text gives no hint that she is confused or bewildered by what happened.
explanation.B: Correct. Bilal did better than she had warned he might, and she shakes his hand, so she is impressed by his performance.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Her strong reaction to "how well he had done" shows interest, not boredom.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Bilal did well and she shakes his hand; nothing suggests she is irritated by his success.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In the 1930s, architect Frank Lloyd Wright designed a house called Fallingwater for a family in rural Pennsylvania. Instead of placing it beside the waterfall the family loved, he built it directly over the falls, with stone floors that stretch out above the stream. Wright used local sandstone and let a boulder rise through the living room floor, all to help the house ______ with the forest and rock around it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: blend
choices.B: trade
choices.C: interfere
choices.D: compete

explanation.why: Wright built over the falls, used "local sandstone," and even let a natural boulder rise through the floor. These choices tie the house to its natural setting, so the blank needs a word meaning "fit in smoothly." "Blend" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Local stone and a natural boulder inside the house help it blend with, or fit naturally into, "the forest and rock around it."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A house cannot trade with a forest, and nothing in the text is about exchanging anything.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Wright's choices are meant to join the house to the landscape, the opposite of disturbing or interfering with it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Using the site's own stone and boulder makes the house part of its setting; it does not set the house against the forest.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In winter, food is scarce for American black bears, so many spend months in their dens without eating or drinking. During this time, a bear's heart rate can drop to a small fraction of its normal rate, and its breathing slows as well. By slowing its body down in these ways, the bear ______ the fat it stored up in the fall, making that supply last until spring.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: squanders
choices.B: replenishes
choices.C: conserves
choices.D: displays

explanation.why: The bear eats nothing for months, so it must live on stored fat. Slowing its heart and breathing uses less energy, "making that supply last until spring." Using something carefully so it lasts is conserving it, so "conserves" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. To squander is to waste, the opposite of making the fat supply "last until spring."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The bear is not eating, so it cannot replenish, or refill, its fat supply during the winter; it can only use it slowly.
explanation.C: Correct. By slowing its body, the bear uses its stored fat slowly and makes it last, which is what "conserves" means.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text is about how the bear uses its fat, not about showing it off.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Viking longships, used in Scandinavia from about 800 to 1100 CE, were built for more than ocean crossings. Their hulls were remarkably ______, often sitting only about a meter deep in the water even when the ships were loaded. As a result, Viking crews could row far up rivers into the heart of Europe and run their ships right onto beaches where there was no harbor.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: deep
choices.B: shallow
choices.C: heavy
choices.D: decorated

explanation.why: The hulls sat "only about a meter deep in the water," which let the ships travel up rivers and land on beaches. A hull that does not reach far below the surface is shallow, so "shallow" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A deep hull would run aground in rivers and on beaches, the opposite of what the text describes.
explanation.B: Correct. Sitting "only about a meter deep," the hulls were shallow, which let crews row up rivers and onto beaches.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A heavy, loaded ship would sink deeper into the water; the text stresses how little of the hull was below the surface.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about decoration; it explains how the hull's shape let the ships reach rivers and beaches.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Asiatic lions once roamed across much of western and southern Asia, but by the early 1900s hunting had reduced them to a small group in the Gir Forest of Gujarat, India. Since then, strict protection of the forest has allowed the population to ______. An official count found about 180 lions in 1968, and by 2020 the number had grown to more than 670.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: recover
choices.B: migrate
choices.C: disappear
choices.D: decline

explanation.why: After hunting had left only "a small group," protection allowed the numbers to rise from about 180 to more than 670. A population that grows back after falling very low is recovering, so "recover" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Protection let a population that hunting had cut to "a small group" grow back to more than 670, so it was able to recover.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the lions survive in the Gir Forest and gives no sign that they moved somewhere else.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The lions did not disappear; the count rose to more than 670.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The count went up from about 180 to more than 670, so the population grew rather than declined.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The steelpan, the national instrument of Trinidad and Tobago, began as a kind of recycling. In the 1930s and 1940s, musicians in Trinidad took steel oil drums that had been ______ after use and hammered their tops into shallow bowls. They shaped each bowl into dented sections that ring at different pitches, so a drum nobody wanted became an instrument capable of playing full melodies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: discarded
choices.B: purchased
choices.C: decorated
choices.D: refurbished

explanation.why: The text calls the steelpan's beginning "a kind of recycling" and later describes the oil drum as one "nobody wanted." A container that was thrown away after use is discarded, so "discarded" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. "Recycling" and "a drum nobody wanted" show that the drums had been thrown away, or discarded, after use.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes the drums as unwanted objects that were recycled; nothing suggests the musicians bought them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not mention decorating the drums; it says they were unwanted until musicians reshaped them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing says the drums were restored to good condition before the musicians got them; the text says "nobody wanted" them.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Leila dreaded the nine-hour train ride to her aunt's town, mostly because her two little brothers would be sitting beside her. She expected them to complain the whole way. Instead, they pressed their faces to the window, counted cows and bridges, and invented a game in which every passing station was a new planet to explore. When the train finally pulled in, Leila was surprised to find that the trip had been ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: uncomfortable
choices.B: tedious
choices.C: silent
choices.D: delightful

explanation.why: Leila expected complaints, but "Instead" her brothers played happy games all the way. She is "surprised" at how the trip turned out, so it must have been better than she feared. "Delightful" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text describes the trip as unpleasant, and Leila's surprise shows the trip turned out better than she feared, not worse.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Tedious" means boring, which is what Leila expected. She is "surprised," so the trip must have been different from what she feared.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The brothers were counting out loud and playing games; nothing suggests the trip was quiet.
explanation.D: Correct. The brothers' games turned a ride Leila "dreaded" into a fun one, so she is surprised to find it was delightful.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In ancient Mesopotamia, people often carried a cylinder seal, a small stone tube carved with a picture or pattern. When the seal was rolled across wet clay, it left a raised image. Because the design on each person's seal was ______, the image worked much like a signature: officials and merchants pressed it onto contracts, letters, and sealed jars to show who had approved or owned them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: interchangeable
choices.B: fragile
choices.C: ancient
choices.D: distinctive

explanation.why: The image worked "much like a signature," showing "who had approved or owned" something. A mark can identify one person only if it is different from everyone else's, so the blank needs a word like "distinctive."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Interchangeable designs, ones that could be swapped for one another, could not show who approved or owned something; it would not work like a signature.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Whether the seal could break has nothing to do with why its image could identify a person.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The seals are ancient to us today, but age does not explain why an image could identify one particular person.
explanation.D: Correct. Each person's design was distinctive, or different from others, so the image could show who had approved or owned an item, just as a signature does.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Diamond and graphite are both made of nothing but carbon atoms, yet the two materials could hardly be more ______. Diamond, in which each atom is locked tightly to four neighbors, is the hardest natural substance known. Graphite, whose atoms form flat sheets that slide easily over one another, is so soft that it leaves marks on paper and is used in pencils.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: comparable
choices.B: common
choices.C: different
choices.D: valuable

explanation.why: "Yet" signals a contrast with the fact that both materials are made of the same atoms. The rest of the text shows diamond as extremely hard and graphite as very soft. The blank must stress how unlike each other they are, so "different" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Yet" sets up a contrast with their shared makeup, and the text goes on to show that one is very hard and the other very soft. "Comparable" says the opposite.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how common either material is.
explanation.C: Correct. Though made of the same atoms, diamond is the hardest natural substance and graphite is soft enough to use in pencils, so they could hardly be more different.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text compares hardness and softness, not worth, and it never says graphite is valuable.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Kalamkari is a textile art from southern India whose name means roughly "pen work." In its traditional hand-drawn style, artists sketch each design freehand on cotton cloth with a pen cut from bamboo, then fill it in with dyes made from plants and minerals. Because every line is drawn by hand rather than printed by a machine, no two pieces of kalamkari are exactly ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: old
choices.B: alike
choices.C: costly
choices.D: bright

explanation.why: Each design is drawn "freehand," and every line is made "by hand rather than printed by a machine." Hand drawing always varies a little, so the pieces cannot be identical. "Alike" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Hand drawing has nothing to do with a piece's age, and the text never discusses when pieces were made.
explanation.B: Correct. Because each line is drawn by hand, every piece varies slightly, so no two are exactly alike.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about price; hand drawing explains why pieces differ from one another, not what they cost.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not discuss how bright the colors are, and hand drawing would not explain a difference in brightness.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Li Na wanted to finish her calligraphy practice quickly so she could go outside. Her grandfather, however, would not let her rush. He showed her the same stroke again and again, waited quietly while she tried it, and never raised his voice when ink blotted the page. Each time she failed, he simply laid a fresh sheet in front of her. He was the most ______ teacher Li Na had ever had.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: talkative
choices.B: hurried
choices.C: forgetful
choices.D: patient

explanation.why: The grandfather repeats the same stroke "again and again," waits "quietly," never raises his voice, and calmly gives Li Na a fresh sheet after each failure. Someone who stays calm through repeated mistakes is patient, so "patient" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The grandfather "waited quietly" and "simply" handed over a new sheet; he is not described as talking much.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It is Li Na who wants to rush; her grandfather "would not let her" and takes his time.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing suggests the grandfather forgets anything; he repeats the stroke on purpose.
explanation.D: Correct. Calmly repeating the lesson and offering a fresh sheet after every failure shows a patient teacher.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Farming in ancient Egypt depended on the yearly flood of the Nile River, which spread water and rich soil across the fields. To track the flood, officials used nilometers: stone staircases or pillars marked with measured levels. A flood that reached the right height usually meant a large harvest, so officials used the readings to ______ how much grain farmers would grow and to set taxes accordingly.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: remember
choices.B: predict
choices.C: ignore
choices.D: celebrate

explanation.why: The flood came before the harvest, and its height "usually meant" a certain kind of harvest. Officials could therefore use the readings to judge in advance how much grain would be grown. Judging something ahead of time is predicting it, so "predict" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The harvest had not happened yet when the flood was measured, so there was nothing to remember.
explanation.B: Correct. Because the flood level signaled what the harvest would be, officials used it to predict, or estimate in advance, how much grain farmers would grow.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Officials "used the readings" to set taxes, so they paid close attention to the harvest estimate rather than ignoring it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes a practical use of the readings, setting taxes, not a celebration.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Polar bears look white, but their fur is not actually white at all. Each outer hair is ______, containing no pigment, and is hollow at its core. The hairs appear white for the same reason snow does: they scatter all colors of visible light. Beneath this coat, a polar bear's skin is black.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: thick
choices.B: colorless
choices.C: multicolored
choices.D: dark

explanation.why: The text says the fur is "not actually white" and that each hair contains "no pigment," the substance that gives things color. A hair without any color of its own is colorless, so "colorless" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not discuss how thick the hairs are; the phrase "containing no pigment" shows the blank is about color.
explanation.B: Correct. A hair with "no pigment" has no color of its own; it only looks white because it scatters light, so it is colorless.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A hair with "no pigment" has no color of its own, let alone many colors.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A hair "containing no pigment" cannot be dark. It is the bear's skin, not its hair, that is black.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Commedia dell'arte, a popular form of theater in sixteenth-century Italy, did not use full written scripts. Troupes worked from a short outline of the plot that was often pinned up backstage. Each actor played the same masked character for years and knew that character's jokes and habits well, so performers could ______ their lines on the spot, changing them to suit each audience.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: whisper
choices.B: transcribe
choices.C: improvise
choices.D: memorize

explanation.why: The troupes had no "full written scripts," only a plot outline, and actors made up their lines "on the spot" to suit each audience. Making something up in the moment is improvising, so "improvise" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how loudly actors spoke; it is about where their words came from.
explanation.B: Incorrect. To transcribe is to write words down, but the text stresses that the troupes did not use written scripts and made up their lines "on the spot."
explanation.C: Correct. Actors who knew their characters well could invent, or improvise, their lines on the spot from a plot outline.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no full scripts, there were no written lines to memorize, and the lines changed "on the spot."

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: For centuries, sailors carrying cotton, pepper, and other goods between India, Arabia, and East Africa relied on the monsoon winds of the Indian Ocean. From about May to September the winds blow mostly from the southwest, and from about November to March mostly from the northeast. Because the winds shifted direction so ______ each year, captains could plan their voyages months in advance and know when to sail home.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: rarely
choices.B: regularly
choices.C: quietly
choices.D: unpredictably

explanation.why: The text gives the same months each year for each wind direction, and captains could plan "months in advance." Planning that far ahead is possible only if the change happens on a dependable schedule, so "regularly" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The winds shifted direction twice every year, so the shift was not rare.
explanation.B: Correct. The winds changed direction at about the same times every year, so they shifted regularly, letting captains plan voyages "months in advance."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about the sound of the winds; it is about their timing.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Unpredictable shifts would make planning months ahead impossible, the opposite of what the text describes.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The shelves in Abuela Rosa's kitchen were crowded with dozens of jars, none of them labeled, and many filled with spices that looked almost the same. On his first visit, Mateo wondered how she could cook anything in such confusion. Yet whenever she needed cumin or cloves, she reached for the right jar without even looking. The disorder, Mateo realized, was only ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: dangerous
choices.B: apparent
choices.C: temporary
choices.D: expensive

explanation.why: The kitchen looks confusing, "yet" Rosa always finds the right jar without looking. So the kitchen only seems disorganized; to her, it is perfectly ordered. Something that only seems to be true is apparent, so "apparent" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text gives no sign that the crowded shelves put anyone at risk.
explanation.B: Correct. The kitchen looked disorganized, but Rosa's ability to find every spice shows the disorder only seemed real, so it was only apparent.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing suggests the jars will soon be organized. Mateo's realization comes from seeing Rosa find every jar, not from any change in the kitchen.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about cost; it is about whether the kitchen is truly disorganized.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most people picture deserts as hot and sandy, but scientists define a desert by how little rain or snow falls there, not by its temperature. By that measure, the interior of Antarctica is one of the largest deserts on Earth. Although the continent is buried under thick ice, its high central plateau receives only a few centimeters of ______ in a typical year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: attention
choices.B: wind
choices.C: precipitation
choices.D: sunlight

explanation.why: The text says scientists define a desert "by how little rain or snow falls there." Antarctica's interior counts as a desert "by that measure," so the blank must name rain and snow. The word for rain, snow, and other water falling from the sky is "precipitation."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence describes a physical amount measured in centimeters, not how much interest people pay to the region.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text's definition of a desert is about rain and snow; wind has nothing to do with it.
explanation.C: Correct. Because a desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, the blank must refer to precipitation, which Antarctica's plateau receives only a few centimeters of each year.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Sunlight is not measured in centimeters, and the text says a desert is defined by rain or snow, not by light.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The earliest daguerreotypes, one of the first practical forms of photography, were introduced in 1839, and a single portrait could require an exposure lasting several minutes. Anyone who moved during that time would appear as a blur. Studios therefore supplied hidden metal stands to brace a sitter's head and neck, helping the person remain ______ until the image was complete.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: hidden
choices.B: motionless
choices.C: distant
choices.D: cheerful

explanation.why: Anyone who moved during the long exposure "would appear as a blur," so studios used stands to brace the sitter's head. The purpose of the brace was to keep the person from moving, so "motionless" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It was the stands that were hidden; the sitter had to appear clearly in the portrait.
explanation.B: Correct. Movement caused blur, so the stands helped sitters stay motionless during the long exposure.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text concerns how far the sitter was from the camera.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The problem the text describes is movement causing blur, not the sitter's mood.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In the early 1900s, a horse in Berlin named Clever Hans drew crowds by tapping out the answers to arithmetic problems with his hoof. His owner was not deliberately cheating, and many observers took the horse's correct answers as clear evidence that he could count. In 1907, however, psychologist Oskar Pfungst showed that this evidence was ______: Hans answered correctly only when his questioner knew the answer and stood where Hans could see him, because the horse was responding to tiny, unintentional movements of the questioner's head and body.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: misleading
choices.B: overwhelming
choices.C: fabricated
choices.D: unrecorded

explanation.why: The correct answers were real, and the owner "was not deliberately cheating," yet Pfungst showed the answers did not prove the horse could count: Hans was reading the questioner's unintended movements. Evidence that is genuine but points people to the wrong conclusion is misleading, so "misleading" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Hans really did tap the right answers, but because he was reading the questioner's movements, the answers led observers to a false conclusion about his ability to count. The evidence was misleading.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "However" signals that Pfungst undercut the evidence; calling it overwhelming would mean it strongly proved the horse could count.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Fabricated" means deliberately made up, but the text says the owner "was not deliberately cheating." The answers were real; they just did not mean what observers thought.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says crowds watched Hans answer and that Pfungst studied when he answered correctly; nothing suggests the evidence went unrecorded.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the late 1600s, brightly printed cotton cloth from India, known in England as calico, became wildly popular among English buyers, who prized it for being light, washable, and colorful. English wool and silk weavers did not share this enthusiasm. They complained that the imported fabric was taking away their customers and staged angry protests in London. To these weavers, Indian cotton was above all a ______, and Parliament eventually passed laws restricting its sale.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: luxury
choices.B: threat
choices.C: novelty
choices.D: model

explanation.why: The text contrasts buyers, who loved calico, with weavers, who "did not share this enthusiasm." The weavers believed the fabric was "taking away their customers" and protested against it. Something seen as endangering one's livelihood is a threat, so "threat" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Buyers may have prized calico, but the blank describes how the weavers saw it. To them it was a danger to their trade, not a fine thing to own.
explanation.B: Correct. The weavers believed the imports were "taking away their customers" and protested, so to them Indian cotton was above all a threat to their livelihood.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A novelty is something interesting because it is new. That does not explain why the weavers complained and protested; their concern was the loss of customers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A model is something to copy or admire, but the weavers protested against the fabric rather than admiring it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When his daughter asked whether he minded selling the old fishing boat, Henrik shrugged and said it was only wood and paint. He had not taken it out in years, he pointed out, and someone else might as well use it. Yet every evening that week he walked down to the harbor to check its ropes, and on the morning the buyer came, Ingrid found him polishing its brass fittings one last time. His claim of indifference, she decided, had been ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: contagious
choices.B: genuine
choices.C: practical
choices.D: pretended

explanation.why: Henrik says the boat is "only wood and paint," but "Yet" introduces actions that show he cares deeply: checking its ropes every evening and polishing it one last time. His claim not to care was therefore not sincere. A show of feeling that hides one's real feeling is pretended, so "pretended" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests that Henrik's attitude spread to anyone else.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Henrik's daily visits and final polishing show that he cared about the boat, so his claim of not caring was not genuine.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Henrik gives a practical-sounding reason for selling, but Ingrid's conclusion is based on his behavior, which shows that his indifference was not real; whether his reasoning was sensible is not the point.
explanation.D: Correct. Henrik's actions contradict his words, so Ingrid concludes that his indifference was only pretended.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Visitors who look closely at the gold mosaics in many Byzantine churches notice that the surface is far from smooth: the small glass tiles, or tesserae, sit at slightly different angles instead of lying perfectly flat. It would be easy to blame careless workers. Yet the unevenness was ______. Because each tile tilts a little differently, it catches candlelight or sunlight at its own angle, so the walls appear to shimmer as a viewer moves through the building.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: costly
choices.B: accidental
choices.C: intentional
choices.D: unnoticeable

explanation.why: The text raises the idea that "careless workers" caused the uneven surface, then rejects it with "Yet." The next sentence explains the effect the tilted tiles create: the walls "shimmer." The unevenness served a purpose, so it was done on purpose. "Intentional" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Gold glass tiles may have been expensive, but the sentence answers whether the uneven surface was a mistake, and the following sentence explains its purpose, not its price.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Accidental" matches the careless-workers explanation that "Yet" rejects.
explanation.C: Correct. The tilted tiles make the walls shimmer, so the unevenness was intentional, a deliberate choice rather than a mistake.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text opens by saying that visitors "notice" the uneven surface, so it is not unnoticeable.

items.subject: science
