items.passage: In 1324, Mansa Musa, the ruler of the Mali Empire in West Africa, traveled to Mecca with thousands of followers and camels loaded with gold. Along the way, he spent and gave away so much gold in Cairo that its value there fell for years afterward. Reports of his ______ spending spread as far as Europe, where a mapmaker in 1375 pictured him holding a large golden nugget.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: modest
choices.B: cautious
choices.C: lavish
choices.D: secret

explanation.why: The text says Mansa Musa spent and gave away "so much gold" that its value in Cairo "fell for years afterward." The blank must describe spending that is enormous and generous. "Lavish" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Modest" means small or restrained, which does not match spending that lowered the value of gold for years.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Cautious spending is careful and limited, the opposite of spending so much gold that a city's prices changed.
explanation.C: Correct. Spending so much gold that its value in Cairo fell for years is spending on a huge, extravagant scale, which is what "lavish" means.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Reports of the spending "spread as far as Europe," so it was widely known, not secret.

items.subject: science
items.passage: An old saying claims that lightning never strikes the same place twice. Tall buildings show otherwise. The Empire State Building in New York City, for example, is struck by lightning about twenty to twenty-five times in a typical year, because its great height gives electricity from a storm an easy path to the ground. The old saying, then, is ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: mistaken
choices.B: accurate
choices.C: recent
choices.D: complicated

explanation.why: The text states an old saying, then says "Tall buildings show otherwise" and gives an example of one building struck many times each year. "Then" signals the conclusion that the saying is wrong. "Mistaken" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. A building hit about twenty to twenty-five times a year shows that lightning does strike the same place more than once, so the saying is wrong, or mistaken.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Tall buildings show otherwise" tells you the example disproves the saying rather than confirming it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text calls it "an old saying"; nothing suggests it is new.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The saying is simple. The text's point is that it is wrong, not that it is hard to understand.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Bharatanatyam, a classical dance form from Tamil Nadu in southern India, uses far more than footwork. Dancers also form precise hand gestures called mudras, each with its own meaning: one gesture may stand for a lotus flower, another for a deer. By combining these gestures with facial expressions, a skilled dancer can ______ an entire story without speaking a word.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: silence
choices.B: convey
choices.C: conceal
choices.D: repeat

explanation.why: The text explains that each mudra has "its own meaning," like a word. Combining gestures and facial expressions therefore lets a dancer tell a story "without speaking a word." The blank must mean "communicate," so "convey" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The dancer does not speak, but the gestures do not silence the story. They are the way the story is told.
explanation.B: Correct. Each gesture has "its own meaning," so by combining them with facial expressions the dancer communicates, or conveys, a whole story without words.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Gestures that each stand for something reveal meaning to the audience; they do not hide the story.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text says the dancer tells a story more than once; the point is how a story can be told without speech.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A single dandelion plant can produce hundreds of seeds, each attached to a tiny parachute of fine white bristles. When the wind blows, these parachutes carry the seeds away from the parent plant, sometimes for more than a kilometer. This helps dandelions ______ across large areas, which is one reason they appear in so many lawns and fields.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: rest
choices.B: shrink
choices.C: spread
choices.D: wilt

explanation.why: The text says wind carries dandelion seeds "away from the parent plant, sometimes for more than a kilometer," and that dandelions "appear in so many lawns and fields." The blank must mean "move out over a wide area," so "spread" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence describes plants moving into new areas, which is the opposite of resting in one place.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Seeds carried far away produce more dandelions in more places; the plants grow in range rather than shrink.
explanation.C: Correct. Wind carries the seeds far from the parent plant, so new dandelions grow over a wide area. That is what it means for the plants to spread.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the plants droop or dry out; the passage is about how they reach new places.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Centuries before European sailors reached the Pacific, Polynesian voyagers traveled thousands of kilometers between islands in large double-hulled canoes. They did so without compasses or printed maps. Navigators instead ______ natural signs: the points where stars rose and set, the patterns of ocean swells, and the flight paths of seabirds heading back toward land.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: argued about
choices.B: ignored
choices.C: relied on
choices.D: created

explanation.why: "Instead" contrasts compasses and maps with what the navigators actually used. The list after the colon (stars, swells, seabirds) names those natural signs. The blank must mean "depended on," so "relied on" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text describes no disagreement among navigators; it explains how they found their way.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The colon introduces the signs the navigators used to find their way; ignoring them is the opposite.
explanation.C: Correct. With no compasses or maps, navigators depended on, or relied on, the stars, swells, and birds the text lists.
explanation.D: Incorrect. People cannot create stars, ocean swells, or seabird flight paths; the navigators read these signs.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The shaggy fur of the brown-throated sloth is often tinted green by algae, some of which have been found almost nowhere except in sloth hair. For years, researchers assumed that the algae were simply taking advantage of a slow-moving host. More recent work suggests the relationship is ______: the algae gain a damp, sheltered place to grow, while the sloth may gain camouflage among the leaves and perhaps even extra nutrients when it licks its fur.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: one-sided
choices.B: temporary
choices.C: harmful
choices.D: reciprocal

explanation.why: The text contrasts an old assumption (the algae were "simply taking advantage" of the sloth) with "more recent work." The colon then explains the new view: the algae gain a place to grow and the sloth gains camouflage and perhaps nutrients. Because both sides benefit, the blank needs a word like "reciprocal."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "One-sided" describes the older assumption that the algae were "simply taking advantage" of the sloth. "More recent work" signals a different view, and the colon lists benefits for both partners.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says how long the relationship lasts; the explanation after the colon is about who benefits, not about time.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing after the colon says the sloth is hurt; it lists only possible benefits to the sloth, such as camouflage and nutrients.
explanation.D: Correct. Both partners benefit (the algae get a place to grow, the sloth gets camouflage and perhaps nutrients), so the relationship is reciprocal, meaning it works in both directions.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Grandfather Haruki rarely praised anyone, and when Emi showed him the bookshelf she had built, he said nothing at all. He ran his hand slowly along each shelf, tested the joints with his thumb, and then set three of his own heavy dictionaries on the top board, where they would stay. Emi had taken his silence for disappointment, but she gradually understood that his careful inspection was itself a form of ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: indifference
choices.B: criticism
choices.C: impatience
choices.D: approval

explanation.why: Emi first takes her grandfather's silence "for disappointment," but "but she gradually understood" signals that she changes her mind. His actions explain why: he examines the shelf and then places his own heavy dictionaries on it to stay, showing he trusts her work. The blank must mean a positive judgment, so "approval" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Someone indifferent would not inspect each shelf and joint so carefully, and he puts his own dictionaries on the shelf to stay, which shows he cares about it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is what Emi first feared ("she had taken his silence for disappointment"), but "but she gradually understood" signals that her first reading was wrong.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Haruki moves "slowly" and examines everything with care; nothing suggests he is in a hurry.
explanation.D: Correct. Haruki tests the shelf and then trusts it with his own heavy dictionaries "where they would stay." Emi realizes his silent inspection was his way of showing that he approved.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: On May 29, 1953, Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary became the first climbers known to have reached the summit of Mount Everest. Reporters immediately wanted to know which of the two men had stepped onto the top first. For some time, both climbers ______ the question, saying only that they had arrived together as a team. Not until Tenzing's autobiography appeared in 1955 did the public learn that Hillary had been a few steps ahead.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: sidestepped
choices.B: settled
choices.C: welcomed
choices.D: invented

explanation.why: The climbers responded by "saying only that they had arrived together as a team," and the text adds that the public did not learn who was first until 1955. So the men avoided answering directly. The blank needs a verb meaning "evaded," such as "sidestepped."
explanation.A: Correct. The men avoided giving a direct answer, saying "only" that they had arrived as a team, so the public did not learn the answer until 1955. They sidestepped the question.
explanation.B: Incorrect. If the climbers had settled the question, the public would have known the answer in 1953. The text says the answer came only with the 1955 autobiography.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Saying "only" that they arrived together suggests the men were avoiding the question, not eagerly inviting it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The reporters asked the question; nothing suggests the climbers made it up.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most humans see color with three types of light-detecting cells in the eye, whereas mantis shrimp have twelve or more. Scientists once assumed that so many receptor types must allow these animals to distinguish colors with extraordinary precision. When researchers actually tested them, however, mantis shrimp struggled to tell apart colors that humans separate easily. The extra receptors, it now appears, may help the shrimp recognize colors quickly rather than ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: swiftly
choices.B: vividly
choices.C: finely
choices.D: loosely

explanation.why: Scientists expected the shrimp's many receptors to give "extraordinary precision," but tests showed they "struggled to tell apart colors." The final sentence offers a new explanation: speed instead of precision. The blank must name what the receptors do not provide, so "finely" (with fine precision) fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Quickly rather than swiftly" sets up a contrast between two words that mean the same thing, so the sentence would make no sense.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text is about how precisely the shrimp can tell colors apart, not about how bright or intense the colors look to them.
explanation.C: Correct. The tests showed the shrimp cannot make precise color distinctions, so their receptors seem to support fast recognition instead of fine, detailed discrimination.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Saying the shrimp recognize colors quickly "rather than loosely" would imply that they distinguish colors precisely, which the tests contradict.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: At Ise Jingu, a major Shinto shrine in Japan, the main wooden buildings are rebuilt on a neighboring plot roughly every twenty years, a custom that dates back more than a thousand years. As a result, the structures standing at any moment are never very old. Yet the custom has ______ something arguably more fragile than any building: because each generation of carpenters trains the next during the rebuilding, the ancient construction techniques have never been lost.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: preserved
choices.B: exposed
choices.C: abandoned
choices.D: replaced

explanation.why: "Yet" sets up a contrast: the buildings themselves are never old, but something older survives. The colon explains what: the construction techniques, which "have never been lost" because carpenters train new carpenters at each rebuilding. The blank must mean "kept alive," so "preserved" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Because carpenters pass their skills on at every rebuilding, the old techniques "have never been lost." The custom has kept them alive, or preserved them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Exposing something fragile would put it at risk, but the text says the techniques survive because of the custom.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Techniques that "have never been lost" have not been abandoned; the custom does the opposite.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The custom does replace the buildings, but the blank refers to the "something" that "has never been lost": the techniques. Those are kept, not replaced.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Electromagnetism, which binds electrons to atoms and produces light, seems to have little in common with the weak nuclear force, which acts only across tiny distances inside atomic nuclei and drives some kinds of radioactive decay. In the late 1960s, however, the Pakistani physicist Abdus Salam and the American physicist Steven Weinberg, building on earlier work by Sheldon Glashow, independently showed that the two forces could be ______: at extremely high energies, they behave as a single force.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: unified
choices.B: compared
choices.C: measured
choices.D: separated

explanation.why: The first sentence says the two forces "seem to have little in common." "However" introduces a surprising finding, and the colon explains it: at extremely high energies, the forces "behave as a single force." The blank must mean "joined into one," so "unified" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. If the two forces "behave as a single force" at high energies, they can be combined into one theory, or unified.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The forces can be compared, but that is not the discovery the colon explains. The colon says they "behave as a single force," which is stronger than simply being compared.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about measuring the forces; the finding is about what the forces are, not about how strong they are.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The forces already seem separate; "however" signals the surprising opposite finding, that they act as "a single force."

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Many Roman harbor walls and buildings made of concrete have stood for two thousand years, while some modern concrete cracks within decades. Scientists studying Roman samples have long noticed small white lumps of lime scattered through the material, and these lumps were usually dismissed as signs of careless mixing. Recent experiments suggest a different interpretation: when water seeps into a crack, it dissolves some of the lime, which then hardens again and seals the gap, making the lumps ______ rather than flaws.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: assets
choices.B: accidents
choices.C: impurities
choices.D: decorations

explanation.why: The lumps were "dismissed as signs of careless mixing," but "a different interpretation" shows that they dissolve and reharden to seal cracks. The phrase "rather than flaws" tells you the blank must be the positive opposite of a flaw. "Assets" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. The lumps help seal cracks, so they make the concrete stronger. That makes them valuable features, or assets, "rather than flaws."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Treating the lumps as products of "careless mixing" is the old view. The "different interpretation" says they help the concrete, so they are not accidents to be regretted.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Impurities" are unwanted substances, which is close to "flaws." The phrase "rather than flaws" needs a word with the opposite, positive meaning.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the lumps were meant to look attractive; the point is that they repair cracks.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When the captain asked whether the crew could finish repairing the ship before the storm arrived, the first mate did not answer at once. She looked at the torn sail, counted the sailors still on deck, and studied the darkening sky to the west. Her reply, when it finally came, was measured: the work could be done, she said, but only if no one stopped to rest before nightfall.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word "measured" most nearly mean?

choices.A: deliberate
choices.B: rhythmic
choices.C: hesitant
choices.D: counted

explanation.why: Before replying, the first mate checks the sail, the crew, and the sky. Her answer then gives a reasoned judgment with a clear condition ("but only if no one stopped to rest"). So "measured" here means carefully considered, or "deliberate."
explanation.A: Correct. The first mate weighed the sail, the crew, and the sky before answering, and her reply sets out a clear judgment with a condition. A measured reply in this sense is carefully thought out: deliberate.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Measured" can describe a regular beat, as in music or verse, but nothing in the text concerns the sound or rhythm of her words.
explanation.C: Incorrect. She paused before speaking, but the pause was spent gathering facts. The reply itself is a firm judgment ("the work could be done"), not an unsure or wavering one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. She did count the sailors, but that describes what she did before answering. "Measured" describes her reply, which cannot be "counted." This choice uses a literal sense of the word that does not fit here.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Bats hunt at night by echolocation, producing high-pitched calls and listening for the echoes that reveal the positions of flying insects. Some tiger moths, however, are not defenseless. When they detect an approaching bat's calls, they respond with rapid bursts of ultrasonic clicks of their own. Experiments suggest that in at least one species, these clicks ______ the bat's sonar, causing the hunter to misjudge where the moth is and miss it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: sharpen
choices.B: disrupt
choices.C: detect
choices.D: imitate

explanation.why: "Not defenseless" tells you the moths fight back. The rest of the sentence gives the result: the bat misjudges "where the moth is and miss[es] it." The blank must mean "interfere with," so "disrupt" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. If the clicks sharpened the bat's sonar, the bat would locate the moth more easily. The text says the bat misjudges the moth's position and misses.
explanation.B: Correct. The clicks cause the bat "to misjudge where the moth is," so they interfere with, or disrupt, the bat's sonar.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The moths detect the bat's calls before they click, but the blank describes the effect of the clicks, which make the bat misjudge and miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says the moth's clicks copy the bat's calls; it says what the clicks do to the bat's ability to locate the moth.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: When Satyajit Ray began his first film, Pather Panchali (1955), he had little money and no experience as a director. He shot much of it on location in a Bengal village and cast several performers with little or no film experience. Some producers doubted that such a ______ production could succeed. Yet the film's plain, unhurried scenes of village life won international praise, including an award at the Cannes Film Festival in 1956.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: polished
choices.B: lavish
choices.C: celebrated
choices.D: modest

explanation.why: The text lists the film's limits: "little money," a director with no experience, and performers with "little or no film experience." The producers' doubts were based on these limits, so the blank must describe a small, simple production. "Modest" fits, and "Yet" then contrasts those doubts with the film's success.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The film was later praised, but the producers' doubts came before that success and were based on the film's limited resources and inexperience. Nothing suggests it seemed polished to them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A film made with "little money" in a village with mostly inexperienced performers is the opposite of lavish.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The film became celebrated only after it was finished and shown; the producers' doubts came earlier, when no one knew if it would succeed.
explanation.D: Correct. A production with "little money," a first-time director, and mostly inexperienced performers is small and simple in scale, or modest.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 132 CE, the Chinese scholar Zhang Heng built a bronze instrument that responded to earthquakes. When the ground shook, a mechanism inside released a ball from the mouth of one of eight dragons into the mouth of a bronze toad below. Popular accounts sometimes claim that the device could forecast earthquakes, but that claim overstates its abilities: it could only ______ a quake that had already begun, possibly indicating the direction from which the shaking came.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: prevent
choices.B: cause
choices.C: register
choices.D: predict

explanation.why: The text rejects the claim that the device could "forecast earthquakes" and says it worked only for a quake "that had already begun." The blank must mean "detect or record," so "register" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the instrument could stop an earthquake; it only reacted to shaking.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The quake made the instrument respond, not the other way around, so the device could not cause a quake.
explanation.C: Correct. The device responded "when the ground shook," so it could record or show a quake that was already happening. That is what it means to register one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Predicting is exactly the claim the text says "overstates its abilities." A device that responds only to a quake "that had already begun" cannot predict it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Ginkgo trees belong to a group of plants that was widespread during the age of the dinosaurs. Over millions of years, nearly all of the group's species died out, and by modern times wild ginkgoes survived in only a few areas of China. Since people began planting it widely, however, the one surviving species has ______ remarkably well: ginkgoes now line city streets around the world, tolerating pollution and poor soil that harm many other trees.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: disappeared
choices.B: declined
choices.C: fared
choices.D: evolved

explanation.why: The text contrasts the ginkgo group's long decline with what happened "since people began planting it widely." The colon explains the result: ginkgoes now grow in cities worldwide and tolerate harsh conditions. The blank must mean "done" or "gotten along," so "fared" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A species that now lines streets "around the world" has not disappeared, and "disappeared remarkably well" makes no sense.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Decline describes the group's long history of dying out. "However" signals that the story changes once people began planting ginkgoes.
explanation.C: Correct. Ginkgoes now grow in cities "around the world" and tolerate harsh conditions, so the species has done, or fared, "remarkably well."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Evolution happens over long periods, but the sentence covers only the time since people began planting ginkgoes, and the colon explains the ginkgo's success in cities, not any change in the species.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Saira's aunt had opposed the tailoring shop from the start, warning that their Lahore neighborhood already had too many. So when the shop's first month ended with every order delivered on time and a waiting list of new customers, Saira expected little from her. The aunt studied the account book for a long while, then admitted, in a voice that showed how much the words cost her, that the shop might just survive. It was ______ praise, but it was praise.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: sarcastic
choices.B: hasty
choices.C: grudging
choices.D: lavish

explanation.why: The aunt had opposed the shop, and she speaks "in a voice that showed how much the words cost her." Her comment, that the shop "might just survive," is weak praise given unwillingly. The final clause, "but it was praise," confirms it was sincere. "Grudging" (given reluctantly) fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The aunt "admitted" her view after studying the account book, and the text ends "but it was praise." Sarcasm would mean she did not mean it, which the text rules out.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The aunt studied the account book "for a long while" before speaking, so her praise was not hasty.
explanation.C: Correct. The aunt had opposed the shop, and the words clearly "cost her" to say. Praise given reluctantly like this is grudging praise, though still sincere.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Admitting only that the shop "might just survive" is the faintest kind of praise, the opposite of lavish.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: To a modern viewer, a seventeenth-century Dutch still life can look like a simple arrangement of attractive objects: a bowl of fruit, a glass of wine, a burning candle. Many such paintings, however, belong to a type known as vanitas, in which ordinary objects stand for ideas. A candle burned almost to its base, or a piece of fruit just beginning to rot, reminded viewers that life is brief. For people at the time, then, the objects ______ a serious message about the passing of time.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: conveyed
choices.B: replaced
choices.C: contradicted
choices.D: obscured

explanation.why: "However" contrasts the modern view of these paintings as simple arrangements with their real purpose: in vanitas paintings, objects "stand for ideas" and "reminded viewers that life is brief." The final sentence sums this up, so the blank must mean "communicated." "Conveyed" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. In vanitas paintings, objects "stand for ideas" and "reminded viewers that life is brief," so they communicated, or conveyed, a message.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never says the objects took the place of a message; it says the objects themselves expressed it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Fading candles and rotting fruit support the idea that life is brief; they do not go against it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A modern viewer might miss the message, but the sentence is about "people at the time," whom the objects "reminded" that life is brief. For them, the objects made the message clear rather than hiding it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In many tree species, a new growth ring forms each year, and rings tend to be wider in wet years than in dry ones, so old timber can be used to reconstruct past climates. Skeptics have noted a weakness: a tree occasionally skips a ring or forms two in one year. Such errors can be caught, however, by comparing many trees from the same area. A sequence of wide and narrow rings found in one tree should be ______ in dozens of others, so a ring that is missing or doubled in a single tree stands out.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: mirrored
choices.B: unusual
choices.C: absent
choices.D: enlarged

explanation.why: The text says errors in one tree "can be caught" by comparing many trees from the same area. That works only if the same pattern of wide and narrow rings shows up in the other trees, so a missing or doubled ring "stands out." The blank must mean "matched" or "repeated," so "mirrored" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Trees in the same area grow under the same weather, so they should show the same sequence of rings. If the sequence is mirrored in many trees, one tree that breaks the pattern "stands out" as an error.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The method depends on the sequence being common to many trees. If it were unusual in them, a missing ring would not stand out.
explanation.C: Incorrect. If the sequence were absent from the other trees, there would be no shared pattern to compare against, and an error in one tree could not be spotted.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text says rings grow bigger in other trees; the comparison is about whether the same pattern appears.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The marine bacterium Vibrio fischeri is capable of producing light, yet a lone cell drifting in open water stays dark. Each cell continually releases a small signaling molecule into its surroundings, and only when the bacteria are densely crowded, as they are inside the light organ of the Hawaiian bobtail squid, does that molecule accumulate enough to switch on the genes for light production. The bacteria, in other words, do not glow simply because they are able to; they ______ their glow, producing it only when enough cells are present for the light to be bright enough to matter.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: imitate
choices.B: regulate
choices.C: inherit
choices.D: relinquish

explanation.why: The text contrasts merely being able to glow with glowing "only when enough cells are present." The semicolon sets up a correction: the bacteria actively control when the light is made. The blank needs a verb meaning "control or adjust according to conditions."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the bacteria copy another organism's light; the point is that they control their own.
explanation.B: Correct. To regulate something is to control when and how much of it happens, which matches cells that switch on light production only at high density.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The bacteria may inherit the ability to glow, but the text says they "do not glow simply because they are able to"; the blank must describe how they control the glow, not where the ability came from.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Relinquish" means give up; the bacteria do produce light when crowded, so they do not give it up.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The Icelandic sagas, prose narratives written down in the 1200s and 1300s, describe events said to have occurred two or three centuries earlier, when Norse settlers first farmed the island. Historians once mined them for dates and genealogies as if they were archival records. More recent scholars have grown wary of that practice, pointing out that the authors shaped their material to suit the concerns of their own time. Few, however, would discard the sagas altogether: archaeologists have located farmsteads where the texts place them, and the sagas remain a valuable, if ______, guide to the society they portray, one to be consulted alongside other evidence rather than trusted on its own.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: exhaustive
choices.B: contemporaneous
choices.C: spurious
choices.D: fallible

explanation.why: "Valuable, if ______" grants a strength and then admits a weakness. The text says the sagas were shaped by later concerns and should not be "trusted on its own," yet archaeology confirms some of their details. The blank must mean "capable of error," not "entirely false."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "If" here introduces a limitation, but "exhaustive" (complete, covering everything) is a strength, and nothing suggests the sagas cover everything.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Contemporaneous" means from the same time, but the sagas were written two or three centuries after the events they describe.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Spurious" means false or fake, but the text says scholars would not discard the sagas and that archaeology supports some of what they say. This goes much further than the text.
explanation.D: Correct. "Fallible" means liable to be wrong, which fits a source that is useful but must be checked against other evidence.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The bronze sculptures produced in southern India under the Chola dynasty, between roughly the ninth and thirteenth centuries, were cast by the lost-wax method: an artist modeled the figure in wax, encased it in clay, and melted the wax away so that molten metal could fill the hollow. Because the clay mold had to be broken to free the bronze, and because each casting required a newly modeled wax figure, every piece was ______. Scholars who catalog these works therefore treat apparent near-duplicates not as copies from a shared mold but as separate creations by artists following a common set of conventions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: derivative
choices.B: provisional
choices.C: anonymous
choices.D: unrepeatable

explanation.why: The text gives two reasons that no mold could be reused: the mold was broken and each casting needed a new wax model. The next sentence confirms that near-duplicates are "not copies from a shared mold but separate creations." The blank must mean "impossible to reproduce exactly."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Derivative" means copied from something else, the opposite of what the text says about separate creations rather than copies.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Provisional" means temporary or not yet final; nothing suggests the finished bronzes were temporary.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Many old sculptures are by unknown artists, but the text's reasons (the broken mold, the new wax figure) explain why each piece was one of a kind, not why its maker is unknown.
explanation.D: Correct. Since every mold was destroyed and every wax model was new, each bronze could not be produced again in identical form.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: At the reception after her farewell concert, Ingrid Halvorsen accepted every compliment with the same gracious nod and answered every question about her retirement in the same unhurried voice. Only her brother, standing near the window, noticed that she had turned her wedding ring around her finger perhaps fifty times, and that she laughed a moment too quickly whenever a guest mentioned the orchestra. To the admirers crowding around her, Ingrid's calm seemed complete; to Lars, who had known her all his life, it was plainly ______, a surface held in place by effort.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: contagious
choices.B: genuine
choices.C: habitual
choices.D: studied

explanation.why: Lars sees signs of strain (the ring turned fifty times, laughter "a moment too quickly"), and the phrase after the comma defines the blank: "a surface held in place by effort." The word must describe a calm that is deliberately put on rather than truly felt.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Contagious" means spreading to others; the text is about whether Ingrid's own calm is real, not about its effect on the guests.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Genuine" means real and sincere, but Lars sees that the calm is only "a surface."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Habitual" means done out of habit, which suggests something automatic and easy, not something "held in place by effort."
explanation.D: Correct. "Studied" here means carefully and deliberately produced, which fits a calm that is "held in place by effort."

items.subject: science
items.passage: For decades, estimates of how many fish live in the ocean's twilight zone, the dim layer between about 200 and 1,000 meters deep, came mainly from trawl nets. Acoustic surveys, which measure echoes returned by fish, have since suggested that the net-based figures ______ the true total, perhaps by a factor of ten: many of the small, quick lanternfish and bristlemouths that dominate these depths apparently sense approaching nets and dart away. Acoustic methods carry their own uncertainties, since other organisms also return echoes, but few researchers now treat the older figures as anything more than a minimum.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: inflated
choices.B: understated
choices.C: approximated
choices.D: corroborated

explanation.why: The text explains that fish escape the nets, so the nets catch fewer fish than are really there, and it ends by calling the older figures "a minimum." The blank must mean "gave too low a value for," and "perhaps by a factor of ten" shows the error was large.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Inflated" means made too large, but fish escaping the nets would make the counts too small.
explanation.B: Correct. "Understated" means presented as smaller than it really is, which matches net figures that missed the fish that darted away.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Approximated" means came close to, but an error of perhaps ten times is not close, and the text says the old figures are only "a minimum."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Corroborated" means confirmed; the acoustic surveys challenge the net figures rather than confirm them.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: When coffeehouses spread through Istanbul in the sixteenth century, Ottoman authorities periodically tried to close them, wary of places where men of different ranks gathered to talk. The bans rarely lasted. Historian Selin Arıkan argues that official hostility toward the coffeehouses was less ______ than it appears. She notes that officials who signed closure orders sometimes frequented the establishments themselves, and that the orders were often lifted within months, in some cases after the owners agreed to pay new taxes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: pragmatic
choices.B: implacable
choices.C: intermittent
choices.D: covert

explanation.why: Arıkan's evidence shows that the hostility could be softened: officials visited the coffeehouses and lifted bans, sometimes in exchange for taxes. So the hostility was less unyielding than it looks. The blank needs a word meaning "impossible to satisfy or soften."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Lifting bans in exchange for taxes suggests the hostility was more practical than it appears, not less, so "pragmatic" reverses the argument.
explanation.B: Correct. "Implacable" means unable to be calmed or bargained with. Bans lifted within months, sometimes for taxes, show hostility that was less implacable than it seemed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Intermittent" means starting and stopping. The text already says the authorities acted "periodically" and that bans "rarely lasted," so the evidence does not make the hostility look less intermittent.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Covert" means hidden, but the closure orders were public acts; nothing suggests the hostility was secret.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In much Baroque music, the keyboard player's part was written as a single bass line with small numerals beneath it indicating which chords to play. How those chords were spaced, ornamented, and rhythmically distributed was left to the performer, who was expected to vary them from one performance to the next. Modern editions that print a fully written-out keyboard part are therefore convenient but potentially misleading: they make one editor's choices look ______, when the composer had in fact expected each player to fill in the harmony differently.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: definitive
choices.B: arbitrary
choices.C: anachronistic
choices.D: improvised

explanation.why: The word "when" sets up a contrast between how the printed part looks and what the composer intended. The composer expected each player to fill in the harmony "differently," so the problem with a printed part is that it makes one version look like the only correct one.
explanation.A: Correct. "Definitive" means final and authoritative, which is the misleading impression a printed part gives when the composer expected many versions.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Arbitrary" means chosen without reason. A printed part does not make choices look random; if anything, it makes them look official.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Anachronistic" means belonging to the wrong period. The text's contrast is between one fixed version and many possible versions, not between old and modern styles.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A part that is fully written out looks fixed, not improvised; improvising is what the composer expected the players to do.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Jerdon's courser, a small bird of the scrub forests of southeastern India, was first described in 1848 and was then so rarely recorded that, for most of the twentieth century, many ornithologists presumed it extinct. In 1986, searchers guided by a local trapper finally found living birds in the hill forests of Andhra Pradesh. The species had not vanished after all; it had simply ______ observers, being active almost entirely at night and keeping to dense, thorny undergrowth where few people looked.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: eluded
choices.B: outlived
choices.C: rewarded
choices.D: imitated

explanation.why: The words "had not vanished after all" show that the bird was there the whole time but was not seen. The reasons given (active at night, hidden in thick undergrowth) explain why people failed to find it. The blank must mean "escaped the notice of."
explanation.A: Correct. To elude observers is to escape their notice, which fits a night-active bird hidden in thick scrub.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Outlived" means lived longer than. The point is that observers failed to see the bird, not that it survived longer than they did.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Rewarded" suggests the bird gave observers something for their effort, but for most of a century it gave them nothing to see.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the bird copied anything; its night habits and hiding places, not mimicry, kept it unseen.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When Joaquín returned to Valdivia after eleven years abroad, he had braced himself for change: new buildings, unfamiliar shops, faces he no longer knew. What unsettled him instead was how little had changed. The bakery on the corner still sold the same bread, and the river still carried the same slow boats past the market. It was he who had altered, and the town's very constancy seemed to ______ him, as though every unchanged street were asking where he had been all this time.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: exonerate
choices.B: reproach
choices.C: welcome
choices.D: conceal

explanation.why: Joaquín is "unsettled," and the comparison at the end imagines the streets "asking where he had been all this time," a question that sounds like an accusation. The blank must mean "express disapproval of" or "blame."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Exonerate" means free from blame, but the streets seem to ask where he has been, which suggests blame rather than forgiveness.
explanation.B: Correct. To reproach someone is to express disappointment or blame, which fits streets that seem to ask where he has been all these years.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A welcoming town would comfort Joaquín, but the text says its sameness "unsettled him."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The unchanged town makes Joaquín's own change more obvious to him; it does not hide him or anything about him.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Tiny zircon crystals from the Jack Hills of Western Australia have been dated to about 4.4 billion years ago, making them the oldest known fragments of Earth's crust. Some geologists argue that the chemistry of these grains indicates that they formed in the presence of liquid water, which would push back the date by which the planet had oceans. Others caution that the evidence is ______: the chemical signatures could also have arisen through processes that acted on the crystals long after they formed, so the grains are consistent with an early watery Earth without proving it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: equivocal
choices.B: anomalous
choices.C: compelling
choices.D: fabricated

explanation.why: The colon introduces an explanation of the blank: the signatures "could also have arisen" another way, so the grains are "consistent with" early water "without proving it." Evidence that fits two explanations is open to more than one interpretation.
explanation.A: Correct. "Equivocal" means open to more than one interpretation, which matches evidence that is consistent with early water without proving it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Anomalous" means unusual or out of line with expectations; the text's point is that the evidence fits more than one explanation, not that it is strange.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Compelling" means convincing, but these geologists say the evidence does not prove the claim.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Fabricated" means invented or faked. The cautious geologists question what the evidence means, not whether it is real.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: It is often said that people in medieval Europe typically died at around age thirty. The figure is not invented: estimates of average life expectancy at birth for the period do fall roughly in that range. The average is nonetheless ______, because it is pulled sharply downward by the very high death rates of infants and young children. A person who survived childhood had a reasonable chance of living into his or her fifties or sixties, so few medieval adults would have regarded thirty as old age.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: unverifiable
choices.B: inflated
choices.C: arbitrary
choices.D: deceptive

explanation.why: The text grants that the figure is accurate ("not invented") but says "nonetheless" something is wrong with it: the average hides the fact that adults often lived much longer. The blank needs a word for something technically true that gives a false impression.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Unverifiable" means impossible to check, but the text says estimates for the period do support the figure.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Inflated" means too high, but the text says the average is pulled down, so it makes lives look shorter, not longer.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Arbitrary" means chosen without reason, but the average is based on real estimates and has a clear cause, the deaths of young children.
explanation.D: Correct. "Deceptive" means giving a false impression. The average is accurate yet misleads people into thinking most adults died at thirty.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Michelangelo left several marble figures, the so-called Prisoners now displayed in Florence, only partly carved, so that bodies seem to twist and strain out of rough, unworked stone. Some viewers, assuming the figures were simply abandoned, have wished that a later sculptor had finished them. Yet completion would have ______ the very quality that many admirers prize most in these works: the tension between the shaped figure and the raw block, which invites the viewer to imagine the form still in the act of emerging.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: foreclosed
choices.B: intensified
choices.C: parodied
choices.D: documented

explanation.why: "Yet" introduces an objection to finishing the statues. The prized quality depends on the figures being unfinished ("still in the act of emerging"), so completing them would make that quality impossible. The blank must mean "ruled out" or "shut off."
explanation.A: Correct. "Foreclosed" means made impossible in advance, which fits completion eliminating the sense of a form still emerging.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Finishing the figures would remove the raw stone, so it would weaken the tension between figure and block, not intensify it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Parodied" means imitated mockingly; nothing suggests a later sculptor would mock the works.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Documented" means recorded. Finishing the carving would not record the unfinished quality; it would erase it.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Roman coins and fragments of Mediterranean wine jars found at Arikamedu, on India's southeastern coast, were once taken as proof that the site was a Roman trading colony. Later excavations revealed a more complicated picture. The settlement had been occupied, and engaged in trade across the Bay of Bengal, well before Roman goods arrived, and its craftspeople continued local traditions of bead-making throughout. The Roman objects, archaeologists now conclude, ______ regular contact with Mediterranean traders but not the foreign control that earlier scholars had inferred from them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: foreshadow
choices.B: predate
choices.C: attest to
choices.D: rule out

explanation.why: The final sentence separates what the Roman objects do show from what they do not: they show contact but "not the foreign control" scholars once assumed. The blank must mean "provide evidence of."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Foreshadow" means hint at something that comes later, but the contact is what brought the objects there, so it is not a later event.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The objects arrived through the contact, so they cannot have existed at the site before it.
explanation.C: Correct. To attest to something is to serve as evidence of it, which is how archaeologists now read the Roman objects: proof of trade, not of rule.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The objects came from Mediterranean traders, so they cannot rule out contact with them; they are evidence for it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In many ant colonies, a large share of workers appear to do almost nothing, remaining motionless in the nest for long stretches. Entomologists once regarded these idle individuals as a puzzle, even a flaw in an otherwise efficient society. Experiments in which researchers removed the most active workers suggested a different reading: the formerly inactive ants soon took up much of the missing labor. Their idleness, then, may be less a sign of waste than a form of ______, a reserve that the colony can draw on when its workforce is suddenly depleted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: insurance
choices.B: deception
choices.C: extravagance
choices.D: defiance

explanation.why: The text says the idle ants may be "less a sign of waste" than something useful, and the phrase after the comma defines the blank: "a reserve that the colony can draw on" in an emergency. The word must mean protection against future loss.
explanation.A: Correct. Insurance is protection kept in reserve against a possible loss, which matches idle workers who step in when active ones disappear.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing suggests the idle ants are tricking anyone; they are simply waiting in reserve.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Extravagance" means wasteful excess, which is the view the text says the experiments challenge.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Defiance" means open refusal to obey, but the idle ants readily take up work when needed.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Medieval European world maps such as the Hereford Mappa Mundi, made around 1300, are sometimes ridiculed for their geographical errors: Jerusalem sits at the center, coastlines bear little resemblance to reality, and distant lands are crowded with legendary creatures. Such criticism may rest on a misunderstanding of the maps' purpose. They were designed less to guide travelers than to present a picture of sacred history and Christian belief, and judged by that aim, their distortions are not blunders but ______ choices.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: deliberate
choices.B: inadvertent
choices.C: eccentric
choices.D: provisional

explanation.why: The text says the maps were meant to present "sacred history and Christian belief," not to guide travelers. Judged by that purpose, the so-called errors are "not blunders"; the contrast requires a word meaning "made on purpose."
explanation.A: Correct. "Deliberate" means intentional, which fits distortions that served the maps' religious and historical purpose.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Inadvertent" means accidental, which is what a blunder is; the sentence says the distortions are not blunders.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Eccentric" means odd or unconventional, which is how the critics see the maps; the text argues the choices made sense given their purpose.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Provisional" means temporary until something better is found; nothing suggests the mapmakers planned to correct their maps.

items.subject: science
items.passage: For nearly three decades, the Pioneer 10 and 11 spacecraft, launched in the early 1970s, appeared to be slowing slightly more than known forces could explain. The discrepancy was minute, but because it seemed to resist every conventional account, some physicists entertained the possibility that it signaled a flaw in the theory of gravity itself. A painstaking reconstruction of how heat from the probes' power sources and electronics radiated unevenly from their surfaces ultimately rendered such speculation ______: the uneven thermal emission, once properly modeled, accounted for essentially all of the anomaly.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: controversial
choices.B: plausible
choices.C: untestable
choices.D: superfluous

explanation.why: The colon explains the result of the heat study: ordinary thermal emission "accounted for essentially all of the anomaly." If a known cause explains the slowing, there is no longer any need to suppose a flaw in gravity. The blank must mean "unnecessary."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Questioning established gravity theory was already controversial before the heat study; the study showed the idea was unnecessary, not that it was disputed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A full ordinary explanation makes the gravity speculation less reasonable, not more, so "plausible" reverses the effect.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The heat study did not make the gravity idea impossible to test; it made the idea unnecessary by explaining the anomaly another way.
explanation.D: Correct. "Superfluous" means more than is needed. Once heat explained the slowing, the speculation about gravity was no longer needed.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Historians of medieval crafts have long relied on guild statutes, the detailed rules that specified everything from the quality of materials to the hours during which artisans could work. Yet a rule's existence is ambiguous evidence. A regulation forbidding the use of inferior wool might reflect a standard that members routinely upheld, or it might have been drafted precisely because the offense was common. Historian Mariela Ferraz therefore argues that statutes should be read alongside court records of actual prosecutions; only then can scholars tell whether a given rule ______ prevailing practice or sought to correct it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: predated
choices.B: codified
choices.C: undermined
choices.D: concealed

explanation.why: The last sentence repeats the two possibilities from earlier in the text. A rule might "reflect a standard that members routinely upheld" or it might exist "because the offense was common." The blank matches the first possibility: the rule put into writing what artisans already did.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Whether a rule came before or after a practice is not one of the two possibilities the text describes; court records would show whether the rule was obeyed, not its date.
explanation.B: Correct. To codify a practice is to set it down formally as a rule, which matches a statute that recorded a standard members already followed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A rule that undermined prevailing practice would be working against it, which is nearly the same as the second option, "sought to correct it." The sentence needs the contrasting possibility.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing suggests that statutes hid what artisans did; the question is whether they described it or tried to change it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Nineteenth-century debates over the restoration of medieval churches pitted two philosophies against each other. The French architect Eugène Viollet-le-Duc was willing to complete a building according to what he judged its original design to demand, even if the result had never actually existed. The English critic John Ruskin, by contrast, regarded such work as a kind of falsehood: every crack and patch, he held, was part of a building's history, and to erase them was to substitute a modern idea for an authentic record. For Ruskin, then, the restorer's confident additions were not acts of fidelity to the past but ______ of it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: travesties
choices.B: reconstructions
choices.C: continuations
choices.D: celebrations

explanation.why: "Not acts of fidelity ... but ______" requires a word opposite to faithfulness. Ruskin saw restoration as "a kind of falsehood" that replaces the authentic record with a modern idea. The blank must mean a false or distorted representation of the past.
explanation.A: Correct. A travesty is a false or distorted imitation of something, which fits Ruskin's view of additions that replace an authentic record with a modern idea.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The additions were literally reconstructions, but that word is not the opposite of fidelity; Ruskin's point was that they misrepresented the past.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Seeing additions as continuing a building's original design is closer to Viollet-le-Duc's view, not Ruskin's.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Ruskin condemned the additions as false, so he would not call them celebrations of the past.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Deccan Traps, a vast sequence of lava flows covering much of west-central India, erupted around the time the non-bird dinosaurs disappeared, some 66 million years ago. Most geologists attribute that extinction primarily to the asteroid that struck near present-day Mexico, but a persistent minority contend that the eruptions, by releasing enormous quantities of gas over hundreds of thousands of years, had already stressed ecosystems worldwide. On this view, volcanism did not supplant the impact as an explanation; rather, it ______ the impact's effects, leaving life less able to withstand the sudden blow.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: mitigated
choices.B: preempted
choices.C: compounded
choices.D: overshadowed

explanation.why: The minority view keeps the asteroid in the story ("did not supplant the impact") and says the eruptions had already weakened ecosystems, "leaving life less able to withstand the sudden blow." The blank must mean that volcanism made the impact's effects worse.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Mitigated" means lessened, but ecosystems already stressed by eruptions would suffer more from the impact, not less.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The eruptions did come first, but "preempted" means made the other unnecessary by acting first. The text says volcanism "did not supplant the impact," so it did not take the impact's place.
explanation.C: Correct. "Compounded" means made worse by adding to, which fits eruptions that weakened life before the asteroid struck.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Overshadowed" would mean volcanism outweighed the impact in importance, but the text says volcanism "did not supplant the impact"; it added to the impact's harm instead of eclipsing it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Mr. Thornbury was a man whose generosity was never in doubt, for he took considerable pains that it should not be. No gift left his hands without some account of what it had cost him, and no favor was granted without an allusion, at a later dinner, to the inconvenience it had occasioned. His neighbors accepted his kindnesses as one accepts the weather, without enthusiasm and without complaint, and they thanked him with a warmth that was, on reflection, somewhat ______; for gratitude that must be extracted so persistently is apt to arrive already spent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: duplicitous
choices.B: perfunctory
choices.C: effusive
choices.D: spontaneous

explanation.why: The neighbors accept his gifts "without enthusiasm," and the final clause explains that gratitude "extracted so persistently" arrives "already spent." Their thanks are given because they must be, not because they are felt. The blank must mean "done as a routine duty, with little real feeling."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Duplicitous" means deceitful. The narrator suggests the thanks are tired, not that the neighbors are secretly scheming against Thornbury.
explanation.B: Correct. "Perfunctory" means done only as a formality, which fits thanks that are dutiful but "already spent."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Effusive" means overflowing with feeling, which contradicts neighbors who act "without enthusiasm."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The gratitude is "extracted," pulled out of the neighbors by Thornbury's reminders, so it is not spontaneous.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Cahokia, near present-day St. Louis, was the largest city in North America north of Mexico around 1100 CE, with a population that some estimates place above 10,000. By about 1350, after a long and uneven decline, it had been largely abandoned. Earlier accounts sought a single decisive cause, such as a prolonged drought or a devastating war, but archaeologists increasingly describe the decline as ______: the evidence points to recurrent flooding, strained food supplies, political fragmentation, and gradual emigration, no one of which seems sufficient on its own to explain the outcome.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: abrupt
choices.B: cumulative
choices.C: cyclical
choices.D: inexplicable

explanation.why: The text contrasts "a single decisive cause" with several factors, "no one of which seems sufficient on its own." The blank, defined by the colon, must describe a decline produced by many pressures adding together.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Abrupt" means sudden; the factors listed include "recurrent" flooding and "gradual" emigration, and suddenness fits the older single-catastrophe view better.
explanation.B: Correct. "Cumulative" means building up through the addition of many parts, which fits a decline caused by several factors that were each insufficient alone.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Cyclical" means repeating in cycles; the text describes a city that was abandoned, not one that declined and recovered repeatedly.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The archaeologists offer a detailed explanation, so they do not describe the decline as impossible to explain.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Equal temperament, the tuning system now standard for pianos, divides the octave into twelve identical steps. The arrangement allows a keyboard to play in every key equally well, but only because every interval except the octave departs slightly from the acoustically pure ratio it approximates; the major third, in particular, is audibly wider than its pure form. Earlier tunings had favored certain keys, making them sweeter while leaving remote keys harsh. Equal temperament, in other words, did not eliminate imperfection so much as ______ it, spreading a small error evenly across every key rather than concentrating larger errors in a few.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: eradicate
choices.B: disperse
choices.C: conceal
choices.D: compound

explanation.why: The phrase after the comma explains the blank: equal temperament spreads "a small error evenly across every key rather than concentrating larger errors in a few." The imperfection is still there, but it is distributed. The blank must mean "scatter" or "spread out."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Eradicate" means eliminate completely, which the text directly denies ("did not eliminate imperfection").
explanation.B: Correct. "Disperse" means spread widely, which matches a small error shared evenly across all keys.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the major third is "audibly wider" than pure, so the imperfection is not hidden; it is spread around.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Compound" means make worse. Equal temperament replaces a few large errors with many small ones; the text does not say the total imperfection grows.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A sample of uranium-238 loses half of its atoms to radioactive decay in about 4.5 billion years, a figure so reliable that geologists use it to date some of the oldest rocks on Earth. That regularity, however, describes only the aggregate. For any single nucleus, decay is ______: physics can state the likelihood that the atom will decay within a given interval but cannot, even in principle, specify when it will do so, and a nucleus that has already survived for billions of years is no more "due" to decay than one formed yesterday.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: cyclical
choices.B: deterministic
choices.C: imminent
choices.D: probabilistic

explanation.why: "However" contrasts the reliable behavior of a whole sample with the behavior of one nucleus. The colon defines the blank: physics can give only "the likelihood" of decay, never the moment. The word must mean "governed by chance and describable only in terms of likelihood."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Cyclical" means repeating in a regular cycle, but a nucleus decays once, and the text says its age does not make decay any more "due."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Deterministic" means fixed in advance by prior conditions. The regularity of a large sample might suggest this, but the text says the timing for one nucleus cannot be specified "even in principle."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Imminent" means about to happen, but a single nucleus may survive for billions of years; the text stresses that its timing is unknown.
explanation.D: Correct. "Probabilistic" means describable only in terms of probability, which fits decay whose likelihood can be stated but whose timing cannot.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Nani had never been a woman to argue. When the family gathered in the old house in Rawalpindi to decide whether it should be sold, she listened to her sons' careful calculations, nodded at her daughters-in-law's sensible remarks about the steep stairs and the damp in the back rooms, and said nothing at all. The family took her silence for agreement. Yet it had been entirely ______: by the next morning she had written to the real estate agent withdrawing the house from sale, and when her eldest son protested, she observed mildly that no one had actually asked for her opinion.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: ingratiating
choices.B: acquiescent
choices.C: noncommittal
choices.D: bewildered

explanation.why: "Yet" signals that the family misread Nani's silence as agreement. Her reply, that "no one had actually asked for her opinion," shows that her silence had never committed her to anything. The blank must mean "not expressing or committing to a position."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Ingratiating" means trying to win favor; nothing suggests Nani was trying to please anyone, and her letter suggests the reverse.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Acquiescent" means quietly accepting. That is how the family read her silence, but "Yet" shows they were wrong.
explanation.C: Correct. "Noncommittal" means revealing no decision or opinion, which fits a silence that only looked like agreement because no one had asked her view.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nani acts promptly and speaks "mildly" and with confidence the next morning, so her silence did not come from confusion.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Many migratory birds, including European robins, can orient themselves using Earth's magnetic field, but how they sense it remains contested. One prominent hypothesis holds that light-sensitive proteins called cryptochromes, found in the birds' retinas, undergo chemical reactions whose outcome depends on the field's direction. Laboratory work showing that one such protein responds to magnetic fields when isolated in a test tube has made the hypothesis ______ rather than proven: no one has yet demonstrated that the reaction occurs inside a living bird's eye with enough sensitivity to guide its flight.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: redundant
choices.B: plausible
choices.C: untenable
choices.D: incontrovertible

explanation.why: The laboratory result supports the hypothesis, but "rather than proven" and the colon show its limit: the reaction has not been shown in a living bird. The blank must describe a hypothesis that is reasonable and supported but not established.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Redundant" means unnecessary; the text says how birds sense the field "remains contested," so the hypothesis is still needed as a possible explanation.
explanation.B: Correct. "Plausible" means reasonable and believable, which fits a hypothesis that has some support but has not been demonstrated in living birds.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Untenable" means impossible to defend, but the laboratory evidence supports the hypothesis rather than undermining it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Incontrovertible" means impossible to dispute, which is even stronger than "proven" and contradicts the statement that the question "remains contested."

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Accounts of Japan's Meiji era (1868–1912) sometimes portray the country as having simply imitated the West, importing railways, a constitution, and a modern army wholesale. Such accounts overlook how carefully Meiji officials chose among foreign models. They studied several European constitutions before drawing chiefly on the Prussian one, whose strong monarchy suited their aims, and they modeled the navy on Britain's while organizing the army first along French and then along German lines. Far from passive borrowing, the process was one of ______ adaptation, in which each institution was weighed against domestic priorities before it was adopted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: discriminating
choices.B: indiscriminate
choices.C: superficial
choices.D: reluctant

explanation.why: The text rejects the idea of "passive borrowing" and gives examples of officials comparing models and picking the one that "suited their aims." The phrase after the comma, "each institution was weighed," confirms that the blank must mean "showing careful judgment in choosing."
explanation.A: Correct. "Discriminating" here means showing good judgment in telling options apart, which fits officials who compared models and chose what suited their aims.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Indiscriminate" means done without careful choice, which describes the "wholesale" imitation the text argues against.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Constitutions, armies, and navies are deep changes, and the text stresses careful weighing, not shallow copying.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text shows officials actively studying and selecting foreign models, not resisting them; it never suggests they adopted them unwillingly.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Written versions of the Sundiata epic, which recounts the founding of the Mali Empire in the thirteenth century, can give the impression of a single fixed text. Among the griots, the hereditary bards of West Africa who have kept the epic alive, no such text exists. Each performance adapts the story to its audience and occasion, expanding some episodes and compressing others, while the core sequence of events and the genealogies remain remarkably stable. To treat any one transcription as the definitive Sundiata is therefore to ______ a living tradition: it fixes in place what griots have kept stable only by continually varying it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: ossify
choices.B: revitalize
choices.C: popularize
choices.D: vindicate

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: treating a transcription as definitive "fixes in place" something that stays alive through variation. The word must mean "make rigid and lifeless," turning a flexible tradition into a frozen text.
explanation.A: Correct. "Ossify" means harden into a rigid, unchanging form, which matches a transcription that "fixes in place" a tradition that depends on variation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Revitalize" means bring new life to, but fixing the epic in place would take away the variation that keeps it alive.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Written versions might spread the epic to new readers, but the colon explains the blank as fixing the story in place, not making it widely known.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Vindicate" means prove right or justify; the text criticizes treating one version as definitive, so it does not say this practice supports the tradition.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Mathematicians of the Kerala school, working in southern India from the fourteenth to the sixteenth centuries, found infinite series for the sine, cosine, and arctangent functions, results that European mathematicians would not reach until the later seventeenth century. Some popular accounts therefore credit the school with inventing calculus. Historians of mathematics tend to resist that claim, not because it is ______ but because it is imprecise: the Kerala achievements are undeniable, yet they did not include the general theory, linking rates of change to accumulated quantities, that defines calculus as Newton and Leibniz framed it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: parochial
choices.B: unfounded
choices.C: novel
choices.D: sweeping

explanation.why: The sentence has two parts after the colon. "The Kerala achievements are undeniable" answers the blank, showing what the claim is not; "yet they did not include the general theory" explains why it is imprecise. The blank must mean "without any basis," since the claim does rest on real achievements.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Parochial" means narrow-minded or locally biased. The text does not discuss the motives behind the claim, and "undeniable" achievements answer a charge of baselessness, not bias.
explanation.B: Correct. "Unfounded" means having no basis. The historians do not reject the claim as baseless, because the Kerala achievements are "undeniable."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text concerns whether the claim is new; the evidence after the colon addresses whether the claim has a basis.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Sweeping" means too broad, which is close to the historians' actual complaint that the claim is imprecise. The sentence needs a contrast with "imprecise," not a near-synonym.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Not all movement along geological faults is sudden. In slow slip events, first detected around 2000 by networks of GPS stations in the Pacific Northwest and Japan, sections of a fault creep over days or weeks, releasing as much energy as a sizable earthquake yet producing no violent shaking. Seismologists initially regarded such events as a benign alternative to earthquakes, a way for faults to ______ stress harmlessly. Some now suspect the relationship is less reassuring: a slow slip can transfer stress to neighboring, locked portions of a fault and may, in some cases, hasten the very ruptures it once seemed to forestall.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: accumulate
choices.B: dissipate
choices.C: transmit
choices.D: conceal
